News.title: Widow of EuroMillions winner, 39, who died after being knocked off bike in hit & run says he’ll ‘never meet unborn baby’
News.content:
LOTTO TRAGEDY Widow of EuroMillions winner, 39, who died after being knocked off bike in hit & run says he’ll ‘never meet unborn baby’

THE widow of a EuroMillions winner who died after being knocked off his bike in suspected hit-and-run says he’ll “never meet his unborn baby”.

Anthony Canty, 39, won £1 million in May 2020, weeks after he helped save the life of a police officer who had a heart attack on a bus during the Covid-19 lockdown.



Essex Police said officers were called to Maldon Road in Tiptree, Essex, at 6.30am on May 21 after cyclist Mr Canty was in collision with a black Ford Ka.

He was raced to hospital but tragically died four days later, the force added.



Police said an 18-year-old man remains under investigation and that inquiries continue.

In a heartbreaking tribute released through police on Tuesday, Mr Canty’s widow Kate said he was “an amazing husband and the best dad”.



She said: “I have lost my husband, my two girls have lost their dad, and he will never get to meet our unborn baby. We are all completely broken.”

Kate said Mr Canty was “one of a kind” and they were “so lucky to have him in our lives”.

“The pain of losing him is the worst pain imaginable,” she said.

“Every day feels overwhelming and we are completely lost without him. He was a hardworking, loving family man with the biggest heart.



“He had a heart of gold and would do anything for anyone. If someone needed help, Anthony was always there.

“He was the life and soul of the party and lit up every room he walked into with his big smile, his charm and his character.

“He made people laugh, brought people together and made every moment brighter just by being there.

“Life will never be the same without him. He really was one in a million and one of a kind. He really was one in a million and one of a kind. I still can’t believe he has been taken from us so tragically.”

“I will make sure all our children grow up knowing what an incredible man and amazing dad he was.



“They will know how much he loved them, how hard he worked for us and how proud he was to be their father.”

In April 2020, Mr Canty gave CPR to a police officer after he collapsed while they were on a bus.

The officer was airlifted to hospital and spent five days in intensive care.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr Canty said at the time that he stayed in touch with the officer’s partner while he was in hospital, and dropped off fruit and flowers, and kept in contact after he recovered.

Police are appealing for witnesses to the collision on May 21 this year and are asking for anyone with CCTV, dashcam or other footage relating to the incident to get in touch quoting incident 174 of May 21.

News.title: Is the A31 still closed today? Latest updates after new New Forest fire near Ringwood closes road
News.content:
A VAN fire broke out on Sunday evening and spread into the New Forest, causing significant disruption to a major road.

The blaze meant that the A31 near Ringwood had to be closed in both directions – here’s everything you need to know about the latest.



Is the A31 still closed?

The A31 remains closed in both directions on Tuesday morning, with drivers facing lengthy diversions and delays.

National Highways said: “Teams have assessed the damage caused by the fire and significant repairs are required to the road surface, road safety barrier and boundary fencing. These repairs can only be carried out once it’s safe to do so.”



The westbound carriageway is closed between M27 junction 2 at Ower and the A338 at Ringwood.

Eastbound traffic can’t use the stretch between the A338 and M27 junction 1 at Cadnam.

National Highways described the fire as a “major incident” after it moved beyond the vehicle and into surrounding land.

Its contractors remain at the scene alongside emergency services.

Bournemouth Airport has told travellers to allow extra time to reach the airport, with the A31 a key route in.

Drivers have been warned to avoid the area, follow the official diversion and allow extra time for their journeys.



Car parks near the fire are unlikely to reopen this week, including Bratley View, the Canadian Memorial and Bolderwood.

Anyone with questions can call the National Highways 24/7 contact centre on 0300 123 5000.

What caused the New Forest fire near Ringwood?

Hampshire and Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service received more than 160 emergency calls at around 5.24pm on Sunday, August 9, reporting a vehicle fire on the eastbound A31.

The flames spread to the central reservation before reaching nearby heathland.

Crews from across Hampshire were sent to the scene, supported by firefighters from Dorset and Wiltshire.



The response included 26 fire engines, four water carriers, six off-road vehicles and multiple command vehicles.

Firefighters continued tackling the blaze throughout the night and warned they would maintain a significant presence in the area for the “foreseeable future”.

The fire service said countryside fires can be particularly challenging, especially when crews need to secure sufficient water for the incident.

It has set up a five-mile pipeline to draw water from Hightown Lake in Ringwood, capable of pumping around 1,300 litres a minute.

No properties currently need to be evacuated, although the fire service said households would be contacted if that changed.



The fire service said: “Please follow diversion signs, allow extra time for your journey and avoid the area to allow emergency crews to work safely.”

A firefighter was also overheard telling a police officer: “We want all the cars and people off the carriageway. Unattended cars are basically bombs when they go off.”

Hampshire Constabulary said 23 vehicles had to be abandoned by motorists on Sunday.

Police moved them, and owners have been asked to call 101 to be reunited with their motors.

How big is the New Forest fire?

Deputy chief fire officer Shantha Dickinson told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme on Tuesday: “Our firefighters and all of our emergency responders have been working in incredibly difficult conditions actually for the last 36 hours since the event started on Sunday evening due to a van fire. And we’re likely to be there for some time to come.”



She added: “It currently covers an area of about a kilometre square. So just to put that into perspective, that’s about 140 football fields, so rolling heathland of beautiful countryside.”

In a 6am update on Tuesday, Hampshire and Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service said: “Crews have worked tirelessly throughout the night, a change in wind direction provided a challenge to the firefighting operations but thanks to the efforts of firefighters we are managing to contain the fire.

“We have been using a mix of fire engines and off-road vehicles to damp down and cool the edges of the area involved in the fire to prevent spread and escalation.

“The police drone is being used to enable us to prioritise hot spot areas and manage flare-ups.”

Overnight numbers were scaled back to seven fire engines and support vehicles, with a “large-scale attack” planned for Tuesday.



What is the A31 diversion route?

National Highways has urged drivers not to follow their satnavs and to use the official local diversion instead.

It has also asked motorists to stick to speed limits on local roads and watch out for the New Forest’s livestock, which roams freely.

Westbound motorists should leave the M27 at junction 2 (Ower Interchange) and use the A326 and A35 through Ashurst, Lyndhurst, Allum Green, Hinton Admiral and Christchurch.

At the Iford roundabout they should take the third exit onto the A3060, then the third exit at the Cooper Dean roundabout onto the A338, travelling north to rejoin the A31 at Ashley Heath.

Eastbound drivers should leave the A31 at the Ashley Heath roundabout onto the A338 and continue south towards Bournemouth.



At the Cooper Dean roundabout they should take the first exit onto the A3060, then the first exit at the Iford roundabout onto the A35 through Christchurch, Hinton Admiral, Allum Green, Lyndhurst and Ashurst, before heading north on the A326 to rejoin the M27 at junction 2.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

With amber heat health alerts in force across most of England and temperatures forecast to reach the mid-30s later this week, National Highways is advising drivers to allow extra time, make sure they have enough fuel, and carry extra water and any essential medicines.

With firefighting and road repairs both continuing, anyone travelling between Southampton, the New Forest, Ringwood and Bournemouth should prepare for disruption.

News.title: Exiled dictator Assad sentenced to DEATH by Syrian court after fleeing to Russia in wake of dramatic revolution
News.content:
MARKED FOR DEATH Exiled dictator Assad sentenced to DEATH by Syrian court after fleeing to Russia in wake of dramatic revolution

SYRIA’S toppled tyrant Bashar al-Assad has been sentenced to death after being convicted of war crimes and crimes against humanity.

“Butcher” Assad who lives in Vladimir Putin’s “warlord retirement village” in Moscow was found guilty on Tuesday of premeditated murder.



He and his brother Maher were sentenced to death in absentia by a court in Syria.

The exiled dictator is notoriously torturing his enemies – including children.



Also in sentenced was Atef Najib, the former head of the Political Security Branch.

Najib was in court for the sentence, seen behind bars.



The tyrants presided over a brutal crackdown in 2011, when teenagers were detained and tortured for spraying anti-regime graffiti.

Crimes against humanity in Daraa led to a huge uprising against Assad, leading to the the civil war and, eventually, the complete collapse of the Butcher’s regime.

In 2018, the tyrant launched a terrifying chemical attack in Douma that killed more than 40 people, including children.

He ordered the Syrian Air Force to drop cylinders full of deadly gas onto a three-storey building in a rebel held town.



Harrowing footage showed kids foaming at the mouth after the deadly cocktail was dropped.

In 2023, investigators from the global chemical weapons agency found the regime responsible for the attack that left civilians choking to death in a basement.

One man called Abdulhadi Sariel, 64, lived on the opposite side of the street from where the chlorine cylinders crashed through.

He told the Observer: “No one in that basement came out alive.”

“Their bodies turned to black, their clothes went green and were burnt, they crumbled and stuck to their bodies.”



After the regime crumbled in 2024 thousands of freed prisoners returned to their families with horrific tales of what they had endured in Assad’s jails.

Terrifying footage captured the moment rebels found piles of dead bodies in the dungeons of the hellhole site who had been tortured to death.

One guard called himself Hitler, and, much like the World War II tyrant, he treated prisoners like animals.

To entertain his dinner guests, he would force detainees to act as various animals – whether it be a dog, cat or donkey.

Those who didn’t play their part properly would be beaten, the Daily Mail reported.



One former inmate told of the guards sadism, saying “the dog has to bark, the cat meow, the rooster crow.”

They added: “Hitler tries to tame them. When he pets one dog the other dog should act jealous.”

In the Mezze hellhole, guards would hang prisoners from a fence completely naked and spray water on them on freezing cold nights.

Assad escaped Syria on a Russian military plane at the eleventh hour in 2024 – as he faced arrest and execution at home.

Putin personally approved Assad’s last-minute rescue, which may have used body doubles and decoy helicopters.



More to follow… For the latest news on this story keep checking back at The Sun Online

News.title: Mum-of-four left cop disabled by dragging him along street with Range Rover as he tried to arrest her – but avoids jail
News.content:
ROAD RAGE HORROR Mum-of-four left cop disabled by dragging him along street with Range Rover as he tried to arrest her – but avoids jail

A MUM left a police officer disabled by dragging him with her Range Rover as he tried to arrest her.

Candace De Silva was pulled over by Afghanistan war hero PC Simon Ward because he suspected she was using mobile phone behind the wheel.



When the 37-year-old tested more than three times the drink-drive limit, De Silva told the officer: “You are not f***ing searching me – I am going. You cannot stop me.”

She then put her foot down and sped off as PC Ward desperately clung to the driver’s side window of her 4×4.



The officer shouted “do not try and resist me. Stop the car” as he used his Parva spray to try to incapacitate De Silva.

She eventually stopped in Liverpool city centre after PC Ward had been dragged for around six car lengths.

He was left with permanent injuries to his knee and can no longer work on frontline duties.

The officer also said the burden he believes he is placing on others was the equivalent of ”living a death sentence.”

PC Ward added: “She thought she was above the law.”

De Silva pleaded guilty to causing serious injury by dangerous driving but avoided jail.



She was instead sentenced to 28 months in prison, suspended for two years, after the court was told two of her four children have neurodivergent conditions and suffer with special educational needs.

JPs also heard De Silva – an accounts manager for the Royal College of Physicians – is the sole earner as her husband does not work.

At a previous hearing, she was fined £457 after she pleaded guilty to drink driving and using her mobile phone at the wheel of a car.

Judge Garrett Byrne told her: ”Your behaviour was absolutely appalling. This officer was someone who was acting on behalf of all of us to protect us and keep the roads safe from people such as yourself – people prepared to drink and drive.

”You could have killed him. But there is one matter that weighs in favour of suspending a prison sentence – that you have four children two of whom have special needs.



”Although you did not give them sufficient thought that day, I have to.”

The court was told De Silva had been pulled over at around 4.15pm on September 14, 2024.

Nardeen Nemat, prosecuting, said: “Whilst speaking to the defendant, PC Ward noted her eyes appeared glazed and her speech was slurred and she subsequently failed a breath test.

“PC Ward requested a female officer to attend so that he could search the defendant but was told no female police officer was available to assist.

“The defendant then told the officer, ‘See no-one else is coming. You are not f***ing searching me. I am going. You cannot stop me.’



“She put her key in the ignition of the car and turned the engine on causing the vehicle to move forward.

”PC Ward put hand into the vehicle in an attempt to remove the key to stop it and told the defendant on numerous occasions to stop the car.

”But the vehicle moved forward and the speed increased. PC Ward grabbed hold of the steering wheel to stop himself being dragged under the vehicle and his feet lifted off the road.

“Inside the car was a female passenger and PC Ward noted that there was a female pedestrian with a pram on the pavement nearby. He feared for their safety.”

The court heard De Silva repeatedly hit at PC Ward causing lacerations to his fingers and the palm of his hand.



She was also seen urging a female passenger to assist with putting the car in gear.

After the mum was hit with the spray, she moaned: “You pepper sprayed me. I cannot see. My eyes are burning.”

She also wept: “I just want to go home to my children. I did not touch you. I did not do anything.”

De Silva then injured another officer when she deliberately slumped to the floor while being led inside a police van – causing one of her handcuffs to scratch the cop’s forearm.

In a victim impact statement, PC ward said he is now office-based and is reliant on a metal support brace and crutches to walk.



He told the court he is in “constant pain” and said he was forced to move house due to his injury.

The officer added: “After fighting for my country and its values being a police officer brought me pride. I thought I could make a positive impact on the community and victims of crime. It is now hard to accept that I am a victim of crime.

“I nearly never came home and can honestly say that despite all the situations previously encountered, September 14 was the worst day of my life.

“My hope of a future is not one anyone would want. I am just amazed this woman feels the apologies will undo the harm. That day she thought she was above the law.”

In mitigation, De Silva’s defence counsel Charles Lander said the incident was a “moment of madness”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

As well as a suspended sentence, she was ordered to complete 15 rehabilitation activity days and 140 hours of unpaid work.

De Silva was also banned from driving for three years and will need to take an extended retest before she can have her licence returned.

News.title: Shocking moment car ploughs into private jet taxiing on runway as flights are grounded & firefighters rush to scene
News.content:
THIS is the moment a car ploughs into a private jet on a busy runway, grounding flights and triggering emergency crews.

Footage captures the moment the ground vehicle slams into the Hawker Beechcraft 400A private jet in Milan, Italy.



The vintage jet – which retails for almost £1million – was taxiing across the runway at the time of incident on Monday around 11.20am.

As the Fiat Panda hits the craft swings to the side, crumpling the front of both vehicles.



The passenger-side door and window of the small Fiat were completely destroyed by the nose of the Italian-registered jet, images show.

Airport firefighters immediately rushed to the scene to secure and inspect the twinjet for structural damage or fuel leaks.



The private plane sustained damage around its radar dome and front section.

Emergency personnel assessed the driver, who remained inside his vehicle until the first responders came.



Fortunately no one was injured in the smash.

The event resulted in a temporary 30 minute interruption to air traffic at Milano-Linate Airport.

As many aircraft are scheduled to land or depart simultaneously from the busy airport, two flights were forced to divert to other airports.

ITA Airways from Rome and KLM were diverted to Bergamo and Milan-Malpensa respectively, Geo News reports.

One additional private jet went through a holding pattern and landed eventually.



It remains unclear how the ground service vehicle lost control.

Early reports indicate the driver may have been distracted or have undergone a possible medical event.

Neither theories have been confirmed by officials.

Normal operations resumed at the airport soon after the incident occurred.

Officials are set to examine the aircraft to determine if there’s any structural damage.

News.title: Woman found dead on major UK motorway after driver ‘spotted body’ on hard shoulder sparking 5-hour closure
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

GRIM END Woman found dead on major UK motorway after driver ‘spotted body’ on hard shoulder sparking 5-hour closure

A WOMAN has tragically been found dead on a major motorway – after drivers reported seeing a body on the hard shoulder.

The M55 was closed for five hours after the grim discovery near Preston, Lancashire, yesterday evening.

Officers were scrambled to the busy stretch following a string of reports from concerned motorists at around 10.20pm.

The tragic discovery was later made between Junction 1, for Broughton Roundabout, and Junction 2, for Becconsall Interchange.





An investigation into the woman’s death has since been launched, Lancashire Police confirmed.

The force said: “We were called at 10.20pm yesterday (Aug 10) to a report of a concern for welfare of a woman.

“Ten minutes later at 10.30pm we received another call after a motorist driving towards Blackpool on the M55 reported seeing what they believed was a body on the hard shoulder of the motorway.

“Officers attended the scene, between junctions 1 and 2 near to the Broughton interchange, where very sadly we can confirm they found the body of a woman.

“Enquiries are ongoing into the circumstances.

“The motorway was closed for around five hours.”

It comes just days after road workers discovered human remains on the M67 in Tameside, Greater Manchester.

They made the grim discovery shortly after 11pm last Monday – with the road later closed in both directions.



A post-mortem has revealed that the body is a man between 20-28-years-old, approximately 5’5″ to 5’9″ tall and of medium build.

The grizzly find prompted a major police response as officers worked through the night at the scene.

Detectives are continuing to investigate and establish the circumstances of his death.

News.title: ‘National disaster’ in Colombia after 7.4-magnitude earthquake kills more than 160 & topples buildings as LOOTING erupts
News.content:
A NATIONAL disaster has been declared in Colombia after a mega quake killed more than 160 people.

Hundreds of buildings collapsed as the South American country was hit by a huge 7.4-magnitude earthquake on Monday morning – one of its largest in years.



So far, 164 people have been confirmed dead and nearly 500 left injured, officials said.

The death toll is likely to rise, with many feared trapped under collapsed buildings.



By Monday evening, more than 2,700 people had been reported missing as desperate families posted information about missing loved ones online.

Striking at a depth of 64 miles in Chocó province, the quake was felt across a huge area – stretching for hundreds of miles across western Colombia, as far as Venezuela’s capital, Caracas, 750 miles away, and in Ecuador and Panama.

In Chocó – where much of the area is only accessible by boat, through the jungle or by plane – 13 people have died.

Another 66 have been reported dead in Periera – where the mayor broke down in tears as he told reporters that numbers were expected to rise.



Three people died at the Pereira airport terminal, according to the mayor, and pictures showed rescuers helping passengers trapped on the city’s 11,000ft-long gondola lift.

In ​Cali, Colombia’s third biggest city and home to about 2.2 million people, at least 85 people were killed.



At least 20 buildings collapsed in the city or were significantly damaged, including the paediatric wing of the de Valle University Hospital.

Rescue workers were seen helping a woman and a newborn baby from a fourth-floor window after the quake.

Colombia’s president Abelardo de la Espriella said 1,000 members of the security forces have been deployed to Cali following reports of looting.

City mayor Alejandro Eder announced an overnight curfew on Monday to “preserve security in the city”.



In Manizales, the heart of Colombia’s coffee-growing region, at least five people were killed and 20 houses were destroyed.

One of the towers of the city’s 20th-century cathedral collapsed in front of shocked crowds.

In Quibdó, one of the first deaths confirmed was Jairson Leonel Valencia, the six-year-old son of a local mayor, The Times reports.

President de la Espriella said he had mobilised the entire military as well as police to respond to the quake – deploying engineers, rescue workers and search dogs.



The country’s Aviation Authority reported widespread damage at airports in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura – with all flights grounded.

Across the country, around 1,600 buildings were damaged or collapsed.



Soldiers, rescuers and families picked through the rubble, removing large pieces of concrete by hand down lines of volunteers.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio said America “stands ready to support” the country.

The US Department of State described the disaster as “devastating” and pledged £11.5million to help provide emergency shelter and supplies.

The EU is also providing funding and supporting rescue operations, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said.

One of Columbia’s most famous stars Shakira offered her condolences after the earthquake struck her homeland.



The epicenter of the quake was in San Jose Del Palmar – located some 250 miles west of Bogota, the US Geological Survey reported.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The quake follows two back-to-back 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes in Venezuela in late June.

Those earthquakes destroyed hundreds of buildings and killed more than 5,000 people.

News.title: Trump hidden in catering truck in secret plane swap over Iran threat, reports say
News.content:
Donald Trump secretly swapped planes as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month in response to a possible Iranian threat, US media report.

The US president boarded Air Force One in view of television cameras before being smuggled onto an elevated airport catering truck and transported to a military aircraft, without journalists and some White House staff on board knowing, the Washington Post said.

Officials told the BBC's US partner CBS News that the US had detected a credible Iranian threat to fire a missile at the plane. The White House has not confirmed the secret switch.

Trump had earlier said he was Iran's "number one target" during the summit in Ankara.

The clandestine manoeuvre came a day after the US renewed military strikes on Iran following a breakdown of negotiations between Washington and Tehran to end the war.

Trump had arrived in Turkey aboard a newer Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar, but announced that he would leave on the old Air Force One "for old time's sake".

On 8 July, footage showed him boarding the presidential jet at Ankara airport. But according to the Washington Post, he was then secretly taken to a smaller C-32A military aircraft - a modified Boeing 757 often used by the vice president - via a catering truck which had been elevated to plane level on the opposite side to where he had boarded.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth boarded the C-32A separately using external stairs in an effort to make the flight appear normal, according to the newspaper.

Journalists and some White House staff boarded Air Force One and were reportedly told to close their window shades. They were unaware the president was no longer on board.

Trump then flew to the UK en route to the US, where he reboarded the old Air Force One and was seen descending from the aircraft after it landed at RAF Mildenhall. It is unclear how he moved from the C-32A back to the legacy jet.

News.title: Amber heat health alerts in place for almost all of England as next heatwave hits
News.content:
Amber heat health alerts are in force across most of England on Tuesday as temperatures start to climb again at the start of the summer's latest predicted heatwave.

The UK's Health Security Agency (UKHSA) is warning that significant impacts are likely across social and health care, including a rise in deaths.

The amber alerts are in place until Friday evening to cover high and even extreme temperatures expected through this week.

During the peak of the heatwave temperatures across England and Wales will widely be in the low to mid-30s Celsius.

The only region in England without an amber alert is the North East which has been given a less intense yellow alert for the same period.

It comes after drought officials declared 71.3% of England is now in drought.

News.title: Councils to get more powers to stop vape and betting shops, PM announces
News.content:
New vape shops will require planning permission and councils will get more powers to block new betting shops, under government plans aimed at improving high streets.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said town centres had been "hollowed out" by decades of decline and "for many people, the high streets they grew up with have become unrecognisable".

BBC News has exposed organised crime on high streets across the country, revealing shops selling illegal cigarettes and vapes, selling cannabis and cocaine, enabling illegal working and suspected money-laundering.

The Conservatives and Reform said the proposals would lead to "more empty" shops, without tax relief for other small businesses.

Burnham said the measures will give councils more power to control what businesses open in town centres.

The proposals come as the prime minister embarks on a tour of the UK, with Downing Street saying he will be in "listening mode" during his visits as he works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

The plans announced by the government include:

Changes to planning law which would mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes, or vapes, would need to apply to their local council for permission to open (England only)

Tightening the definition of a vape shop to prevent businesses avoiding the rules by describing themselves as a general convenience store or retailer (England only)

Scrapping a rule known as "aim to permit", which currently restricts councils' ability to refuse new betting shops and 24-hour slot machine shops (Great Britain-wide)

Requiring planning permission for new adult gaming centres, which offer 24-hour access to gambling machines (England only)

New powers to extend closure orders for mini-marts and vape shops found to be selling illegal tobacco or up to twelve months, something previously proposed by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer (England and Wales)

The National Crime Agency (NCA) estimates that at least Â£1bn of criminal cash is laundered through high street stores in the UK each year through businesses connected to the sale of fake goods, tax evasion, illegal working and illegal drug supply.

Burnham said "the rise of vape shops, betting shops and rogue operators have replaced the shops, services, and community spaces that people are crying out for".

He added: "That's not on. I said we would improve Britain's high streets, and that's exactly what we are starting to do.

"We're putting communities back in control and giving local people a real say over what opens on their high street."

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday that many people were frustrated at vape and gambling outlets "popping up even near schools and some of them are linked to illegal activity and crime".

News.title: 'I started in my 20s and made £8,000': Why women are often better investors than men
News.content:
It can be "largely attributed to culture", according to Gillian Fleming, co-founder and managing director of UK-based Mint Ventures, a women-led angel investment firm.

"Men historically have been more likely to make family investment decisions, and women have also historically not owned the balance of wealth, but that is changing now," she says.

"Also, money and wealth creation is not a topic that women often discuss, and we would like to change that."

Teleri says she has noticed a shift of late. "Investing is definitely something that women are talking about more, which is always a good thing," she says. "That's the case with my friendship group."

When women do invest in stocks and shares, analysis by Fidelity International found that over three years its female personal investing customers recorded cumulative returns of 50%, compared with 47% for men. The analysis does not identify the reason for the difference, but why may it be the case?

One possible clue to women's slightly higher long-term returns lies in how often they buy and sell their investments, with Barclays data showing that women trade around half as frequently as men.

News.title: Perseid meteor shower reaches peak: When and where to catch a glimpse
News.content:
The best annual meteor shower has once again returned to our skies, and the Perseids dazzling display is set to peak on Wednesday night.

But skywatchers will be treated to not one, but two, impressive astronomical events within just a few hours of each other.

A deep partial solar eclipse will be also visible in the UK in the early evening before the Sun sets and the stars emerge. While the two events are unrelated, their timing makes for an exceptional night of stargazing.

Astronomer Dr Becky Smethurst said it was "the perfect cosmic coincidence of events".

Here is when to look up and where you will have the best views of the meteor shower.

News.title: Call with No10 gives us hope, PC Harper's mother says
News.content:
Cole and Bowers were sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter in 2020. Under changes to the Sentencing Act made this year, they will become eligible for release from custody next January.

They are in a category of prisoners - those who have committed certain serious violent or sexual crimes - who until now would have had to serve at least two-thirds of their sentence in jail before being considered for release.

Downing Street had earlier warned it would not be possible to exclude "one or two offenders" convicted of manslaughter from the early release scheme.

However, the BBC has been told that Burnham has now instructed his justice secretary to find a way to exclude Cole and Bowers from the scheme designed to ease prison overcrowding.

In a later statement, the PM said he was "increasingly confident" that work to increase space in the prison system "will allow us to reduce the number of people released early".

He added: "And, in the case of the most serious offenders like those convicted of the killing of PC [Andrew] Harper, prevent their early release altogether."

Adlam said the conflicting reports had been making her "more and more angry" and the uncertainty had left her family "in turmoil".

Of the phone call she received, she said. "I think the fact it's actually come from Downing Street, I've got to try and have some faith in it, but at the same time I've got to protect my own feelings."

Thames Valley Police officer PC Harper, 28, from Wallingford, Oxfordshire, died in 2019 when he was dragged behind the getaway car of three teenagers who had fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

Adlam said: "Everybody is watching this. This is obviously extremely personal to us but it's to do with the country as a whole really. This is really vital to get right, it feels like a hash, like a rush job."

Speaking about Cole and Bowers, she added: "They weren't given extreme sentences and I'm only asking for them to do what they were given, I'm not asking for anything more than they were sentenced."

News.title: Trump says it would be 'terrible mistake' to remove Infantino
News.content:
US President Donald Trump says it would be a "terrible mistake" if under-pressure Fifa president Gianni Infantino was ousted from his position.

Trump's backing followed Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) issuing an open letter accusing Infantino of breaking trust "through deception" with his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

Trump's comments mark the first time he has come out in defence of Infantino since the FFE plans came to light on 28 July.

"Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino," Trump wrote on social media.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again."

The 2026 World Cup was co-hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico this summer, with Spain crowned champions after beating Argentina in the final.

When addressing the FFE proposals for the first time on 31 July, Trump said he had not spoken to Infantino about the plans.

Thrive Eternal was expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE.

Thrive is an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner - the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared.

Infantino has a close relationship with Trump and awarded him the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize in December 2025.

News.title: Jewish school heads spend more time on security than education, review finds
News.content:
Headteachers of some Jewish schools are spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than on educational matters, a review into antisemitism in schools and colleges has found.

Sir David Bell, speaking for the first time about his ongoing government-commissioned independent review, told the BBC he had been struck by how many leaders of Jewish faith schools had told him security was their primary concern - and that "sometimes education takes second place to that".

The report, due in the autumn, examines the experiences of Jewish pupils and staff in faith and secular schools and colleges in England.

Sir David said he found that pupils were "subject to regular harassment and abuse".

He said Jewish children and young people "are facing a pressure - and indeed one might say even a crisis - that is not the experience of other communities in this country".

The review is likely to recommend dedicated training for all teachers and improved education about antisemitism for pupils, the BBC has been told.

The BBC has spoken to several headteachers and staff at Jewish schools. All asked not to be named because of concerns over their security and that of their schools.

One headteacher said: "In recent years [security] has become an overwhelming priority and increased a significant amount. There have been weeks where approximately 90% of my time has been spent on security-related matters.

"Security concerns can become one of the many things that headteachers carry with them beyond the school day and, quite literally, can be among the things that keep me awake at night."

News.title: England set to eliminate hepatitis C
News.content:
Hepatitis C is spread through contact with blood infected with the virus, such as by sharing needles with someone who has it.

Donor blood is already screened for it.

It is a silent disease, meaning people often have no symptoms until much later.

Untreated, it can cause serious and potentially life-threatening liver damage.

NHS England says that since 2015, more than 100,000 people have been diagnosed and treated for hepatitis C, meaning the country is already meeting that target.

Another goal - a 65% reduction in hepatitis C-related mortality compared with 2015 levels - has yet to be met, but might be before the 2030 target date.

Around 50,200 adults are living with hepatitis C, figures for England in 2024 suggest.

Estimates indicate 84.6% of those living with hepatitis C have been diagnosed - just short of the 90% target.

The Hepatitis C Trust says England is "on the cusp" of one of the most significant public health achievements in our country's history.

Prof Frankie Swords, NHS national medical director, added: "England is now leading the world in the mission to eliminate this disease and on course to beat the WHO's 2030 target, but we are determined to keep up the momentum and finish the job.

"We are committed to finding and treating everyone who needs support and would urge those at greater risk to come forward by ordering a free and confidential home-testing kit online."

Adults born in Ukraine, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Albania, Lithuania, Bulgaria, Czechia or Slovakia are particularly urged to test, as some may have been infected through medical or dental procedures before 1991.

People can order a free, confidential NHS home self-testing kit, external without needing to speak to a GP.

News.title: GB's Hunt comes of age with European 100m gold
News.content:
Amy Hunt had her coming of age moment as she stormed to 100m glory to claim her first senior international title and deliver Britain's first gold medal of the European Athletics Championships.

Hunt announced herself on the sport's global stage last year with world 200m silver in Tokyo - the first individual international medal of her senior career.

Having backed that up with Commonwealth 100m silver two weeks ago, the 24-year-old would not be denied gold this time in Birmingham.

"I have had such a string of silvers and I was starting to get a bit fed up with it, so I thought it was time for gold," Hunt, who won in 11 seconds flat, told BBC Sport.

"My parents gifted me these gold earrings to finally level up, because I wear all-silver jewellery.

"They said it was time for gold - they left me that note two nights ago - so it made me quite emotional.

"It was definitely time for me to come of age here."

It was Britain's second medal on the opening day of action after the hosts took silver in the mixed 4x400m relay.

Yemi Mary John held off Dutch athlete Myrte van der Schoot on the home straight to bring a British quartet also featuring Ben Jefferies, Charlotte Henrich and Toby Harries home in three minutes 10.47 seconds, behind winners Norway (3:09.62).

News.title: London Heathrow no longer Europe's busiest airport
News.content:
Heathrow has lost its position as Europe's busiest airport to Istanbul, new figures show.

The west London airport said 7.86m passengers passed through its four terminals in July, whereas its Turkish counterpart recorded 8.15m passengers.

The US-Israel conflict with Iran has had an impact on Heathrow's passenger traffic with Middle East routes in July down 20.2% year-on-year.

Annual figures from trade body Airports Council International show Heathrow was Europe's busiest airport from 1996 to 2019. It lost that title in 2020 amid coronavirus travel restrictions before regaining it in 2023, holding it ever since.

Heathrow continues to operate its two runways at near-full capacity and is seeking government permission to build a third.

News.title: Cocaine worth £232m found in banana shipment
News.content:
Cocaine with a street value of Â£232m was discovered hidden in a large shipment of bananas from South America.

The 2.9-tonne (2,900kg) haul was smuggled into London Gateway Port in Thurrock, Essex, on Thursday.

Border Force intercepted the cocaine at the port and removed it from a trailer, before the drugs courier took the empty load to an address near Buntingford, Hertfordshire.

Nine men allegedly connected to the bust were then arrested and later released on bail.

Border Force had been tipped off about the illegal consignment by the National Crime Agency.

News.title: Treasury contributed to woman's death, inquest hears
News.content:
The death of a Treasury worker who took her own life the day after a meeting with her managers was "materially contributed" to by her employers, an inquest has heard.

Chloe Moffat, 26, a personal assistant to a Treasury director, died on 20 May last year, after she was told of allegations she had shared sensitive confidential information about colleagues, which she denied.

Surrey Coroner's Court heard the Treasury did not apply written disciplinary policy which would have made clear that if the allegations were proven, the likely penalty was a written warning, not dismissal.

A spokesperson for the Treasury said it was "considering the findings carefully".

In a statement to the press, Moffat's family said they believed the Treasury failed in its duty of care.

"When she needed support, reassurance and fair treatment, she was left frightened, isolated and convinced her career and reputation had been destroyed," they added.

The inquest, in which a conclusion of suicide was recorded, heard that on 19 May Moffat went to what she thought was a routine one-to-one with her line manager, but a more senior manager was also present.

She was told of allegations she had shared sensitive personal information about colleagues, obtained as part of her job.

Moffat, from London, denied this.

News.title: Vandals target playground before it has even opened
News.content:
A play area that cost more than Â£178,000 was vandalised days before it was due to open.

Knowsley Council leader Graham Morgan said he was "absolutely furious" that every piece of play equipment at the Finch Woods play park in Halewood, Knowsley had been spray painted with graffiti over the weekend.

Trees and safety surfacing were also damaged and rubbish was left strewn across the site, with the cost of the damage estimated to run into thousands of pounds.

Morgan condemned the "mindless vandalism", saying "it is the cost to the community that sickens me the most".

News.title: Antiques stolen in 16th Century manor house raid
News.content:
More than 20 antiques were stolen from a National Trust (NT) property during a break-in last month, it has been revealed.

The silver, pewter and brass items were taken from the 16th Century manor house at Baddesley Clinton in Warwickshire, on 30 July.

The most notable piece of the 25 taken was a Georgian silver salver engraved with the coat of arms of the Ferrers, the family who resided at the house for about five centuries, the NT said.

"We very much hope the objects will be returned, so they can be enjoyed by everyone," a spokesperson added.

News.title: Great-grandad with cancer risks his health to help others on 460-mile journey
News.content:
A great-grandfather with bladder and kidney cancer is walking 462 miles (743km) for charity, despite knowing it could impact his own treatment.

John Eryl Parry, 78, from Pontypool, Torfaen, began his coast-to-coast journey at the UK's most easterly point in Lowestoft, Suffolk, on 21 June, and is due to reach St David's Head in Pembrokeshire on 11 August.

He found out he had cancer after he fell off a ladder and was taken to hospital.

John admitted he had not told his oncology team about his challenge, but said he was warned by a doctor that his body would "change" during it, and it could impact his treatment plan.

The prime minister has vowed to resolve the “long-running injustice” of indefinite jail terms as part of measures to ease prison overcrowding and stop PC Andrew Harper’s killers from being freed early.

Andy Burnham said he is “increasingly confident” that plans to free up prison cells will mean the number of prisoners being released early can be reduced.

Options being considered include the release of “lower risk” prisoners serving Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) jail terms, he said on Tuesday. The comments offer fresh hope for prisoners trapped on the open-ended sentences which were outlawed in 2012.

The Independent has long campaigned for the unjust jail terms - which have left thousands languishing without hope of release - to be reviewed.

In a statement issued on Facebook, he said he has asked justice secretary Alex Norris to fast-track a plan to create more headroom in the prison estate.

The plan will be based “on a range of options”, Mr Burnham said, including “increasing the rate of removal of foreign national offenders from the prison estate to their country of origin; finding an early resolution to the long-running injustice of IPP sentences, which could allow for the release of lower-risk prisoners; and making greater use of the entire prison estate including using the female estate for male offenders”.

He continued: “I am increasingly confident that a more focused approach along these lines will allow us to reduce the number of people released early and, in the case of the most serious offenders like those convicted of the killing of PC Harper, prevent their early release altogether.”

The development comes as the government faces legal action over the jail terms after the United Nations found Britain is unlawfully detaining a number of over-tariff IPP prisoners in a scathing legal opinion issued last month.

The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention called for Britain to urgently act in relation to five men handed the jail terms, warning their detention beyond their original tariff amounts to arbitrary detention under international human rights law and they are entitled to compensation.

Lawyers are now preparing to submit a rare habeas corpus legal challenge to the High Court, which will force the government to justify the prisoners' continued incarceration to senior judges.

The open-ended punishments were scrapped in 2012, but not retrospectively, leaving thousands languishing in prison without a release date for years beyond their tariff, including some for minor crimes. Once released, many find themselves trapped in a cycle of indefinite recall for minor breaches of strict licence conditions.

Despite 96 prisoners taking their own lives in custody after losing hope of ever getting out, successive governments have resisted calls to resentence those still on the jail term.

More follows on the breaking news story...

News.content:

With another heatwave on the way amid a summer of record-breaking temperatures, it’s likely you’ve considered investing in a longer-term cooling solution as opposed to a quick fix.

According to Simon Bones, a leading sustainability expert and founder of Genous, a company helping homeowners retrofit their homes for a greener future, there’s been renewed interest in the matter, particularly this summer.

“Dramatically so… either for air conditioning on its own (which we actually don’t do), or in combination with other kinds of renewables, where people are thinking about things like heat pumps.

“They’re increasingly asking, ‘can it cool too?’. So I would say it’s been dramatically different from what we would be getting any other time of year.”

In answer to the question, Bones says some heat pumps can cool, if configured correctly. “It can get quite complicated, but you’ve got various options.”

open image in gallery When it comes to electricity-consuming items such as fans or air-conditioning, Bones says these can be effective, but use a lot of power ( PA )

Incorporating renewables

When it comes to electricity-consuming items such as fans or air-conditioning, Bones says these can be effective, but use a lot of power.

As an alternative, he suggests installing an air-to-water heat pump with underfloor heating which provides mild cooling by flowing cooler water through the heating circuits.

Moreover, he says any cooling takes a lot of energy, so integrating with solar panels is smart. “Generating electricity from solar panels, storing it and then reusing it from home batteries to heat your home from a heat pump.”

open image in gallery Bones says any cooling takes a lot of energy, so integrating with solar panels is smart ( PA )

“And because you can buy it, store it, use it at a different time and generate it yourself, it means you’ve got more control over it. And it’s much lower carbon because heat pumps in particular, are four times plus more efficient than even the best gas or oil boiler.

“And solar panels as well,” he adds. “They don’t consume anything apart from sunlight, so they’re fully green once they’re in.”

Bones also suggests thinking about cooling as part of a holistic renewable strategy. “It’s really about the financial,” he highlights. “Running air conditioning, they’re powerful units and reasonably expensive.

“And if you’re thinking about using solar panels, they generate power more when it’s hot and sunny, and therefore you’re aligning your production with your demand.”

open image in gallery Bones suggests thinking about cooling as part of a holistic renewable strategy ( PA )

He says they also deflect some of the heat from the roof as a side-benefit, “but on a day like today, the sun is shining and people have air conditioning”.

This means they can help power those active cooling technologies, and reduce the cost of the electricity they need to buy.

Reducing heat gain

Other practical tips for staying cool include insulating lofts, and reducing solar gain from windows.

Bones says to make sure your loft is well insulated (if you have one), to reduce heat coming in. “If you’ve got poor insulation, most people think that’s about heat oil escaping in the winter.

“But the opposite is true. So the loft space will typically, in a normal house, be really hot in the summer. And if you’ve got poor insulation between the loft and your ceiling, that heat comes down through the ceiling as well.”

open image in gallery Bones says even normal double-glazing lets in less heat and sunshine energy – helping to keep heat in during the winter ( PA )

He also suggests reducing solar gain from windows. Think triple-glazed windows or those with coatings, though Bones says even normal double-glazing lets in less heat and sunshine energy – helping to keep heat in during the winter.

“If you’ve got windows that face into the sun, the more layers of glazing you have, the less that sunlight comes in. So single glazed windows, you’ll get a lot of heat transfer through from what we call solar gain from the sunshine; triple glazing less so.

“Triple glazing is also a better insulator for different reasons in the winter,” highlights Bones. “So performance glazing generally keeps your house a little cooler in the summer, and warmer in the winter.

“Probably not something most people do purely for that reason,” he underlines. “Financially, glazing is expensive, whereas loft insulation, which we’ve just talked about, is much cheaper.”

And while it feels like the longest heatwave on record, there are still some weeks to go…

“It certainly feels quite long, but I’m sure we’ll all be complaining about the cold weather in a couple of months’ time,” quips Bones.

Rod Stewart has been forced to cancel two tour dates after needing an “unforeseen but minor medical procedure” – calling off the first just hours before he was due to take to the stage.

The 81-year-old singer is currently performing dates on his One Last Time tour across the US but pulled out of a concert in Ohio on Sunday (9 August) night, with a post on the venue’s Instagram account explaining: “Due to an unforeseen but minor medical procedure that required prompt attention, Rod Stewart’s performance tonight in Cincinnati has been postponed.”

It said rescheduling was “underway”, adding: “Rod is expected to make a quick recovery and looks forward to returning to Cincinnati.”

The Maggie May singer then cancelled a second gig, which had been scheduled for elsewhere in Ohio on Tuesday (11 August) evening.

A post shared on the Rocket Arena’s social media accounts on Monday (10 August) read: “Following a period of monitoring, doctors have advised Rod Stewart to rest for at least 48 hours.”

open image in gallery Stewart is scheduled to start a Vegas residency later this month ( AFP/Getty )

It continued: “As a result, his performance tomorrow night, August 11, 2026 at Rocket Arena in Cleveland has been cancelled.

“Rod is disappointed to miss the show and appreciates everyone’s understanding. He looks forward to returning to the stage soon.”

It’s not the first time Stewart cancelled concerts in recent months. In June, the singer pulled out of a California gig just hours before his stage time, citing “a diagnosis of an acute upper respiratory infection that has resulted in laryngitis”.

While fans initially sympathised with the star, the support soon turned to criticism when Stewart was spotted cheering on Scotland in the World Cup just a day later.

open image in gallery The singer watched from the stands as Scotland made a historic World Cup return ( PA )

He later admitted it “wasn’t a good look” to attend the game just 24 hours after cancelling a gig, explaining in an interview on TalkSport: “I had to cancel a show the night before because I just had no voice left. But the truth is, I wasn’t going to let my two sons down.

“I promised them since they were born that we’re going to go to a World Cup, and this is the first one that’s come about. And it wasn’t a good look, I admit, but I’m going to just have to take the stick. So, I did it for the boys.”

A week before the California cancellation, Stewart had been forced to pause another concert after nearly fainting on stage.

The Scottish singer is due to perform a six-night Las Vegas residency later this month.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool ‘agree’ Barcola terms, Man City close in on Rodri replacement, Man Utd target defender
News.content:
Liverpool are hoping to swiftly add to the loan signing of Ronald Araujo by hashing out a deal for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola after reaching a reported agreement over personal terms. Barcola leads Liverpool’s list of transfer targets and the Reds are in talks with PSG over a fee, though the European champions are demanding £145m to sell the winger.

Arsenal’s busy transfer window looks set to continue as they move on from their disappointment in not signing Vinicius Jr. They are hunting alternatives in the forward line with Julian Alvarez and the aforementioned Barcola on their list but defensive reinforcements may yet come in the form of Cristian Romero. The Tottenham captain is rumoured to leave Spurs this summer and is eyeing up a switch to their closest rivals.

Meanwhile, Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca – who are considering a second bid after an initial offer of £38m was rejected. City seem to be making preparations for that outcome as they close in on the signing of World Cup breakout star Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille.

Finally, Manchester United are still searching for a left-back with Newcastle’s Lewis Hall seemingly off the table they instead turned their interest on the likes of Antonee Robinson, Jorge Salinas and Joaquin Seys.

Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals with our live blog below

One month after The Salt Path was released in cinemas, an exposé claimed that author Raynor Winn had lied about many aspects of her alleged life story. Now, the film is about to be released in the US – and its lead stars are addressing the scandal for the first time.

Gillian Anderson and Jason Isaacs previously remained silent on the controversy, but are now, bizarrely, expected to do press interviews about the project overseas.

In a new interview while promoting Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma, former X-Files star Anderson said she’d been surprised by The Salt Path’s initial box office success when The Observer’s investigation broke.

open image in gallery Gillian Anderson says ‘Salt Path’ scandal ‘sucks’ ( Getty )

“The film was doing really well in the UK, beyond my expectations,” she told Radio Times, adding: “It sucked, and continues to suck.”

Meanwhile, Harry Potter and White Lotus actor Isaacs appeared on Kermode on Film podcast, when host Mark Kermode asked him: “You made The Salt Path, which is only now coming out in America?”

The actor replied: "It's going to be interesting doing publicity for The Salt Path now that there's been... I said, ‘Are you sure you want us to do publicity?’ They went, ‘Absolutely.’”

Isaacs said he was fine with the decision as he thinks “it’s a beautiful film” and “that much of it is still completely valid”, but levelled: "Obviously, some of the things have been questioned. It's going to be an interesting experience."

open image in gallery Gillian Anderson and Jason Isaacs in ‘The Salt Path’ ( Rialto )

The Salt Path, which was published in 2018 and has sold over two million copies worldwide, details how Raynor Winn and her husband Moth lost their house after a friend invested their money poorly. It charts their fall into homelessness and the long walk that miraculously eased symptoms of Moth’s rare, terminal neurological disease (corticobasal degeneration or CBD).

However, the Observer investigation put this whole narrative into question. It was alleged that Winn had stolen large amounts of money from her place of work, gone into hiding, lost the house after borrowing around £100,000 from a family member, and owned land in France where she and her husband could have lived.

Winn has strongly denied the allegations against her, stating they are “highly misleading”.

open image in gallery ‘Salt Path’ author Raynor Winn was accused of lying about details from her book ( Getty )

“The Salt Path lays bare the physical and spiritual journey Moth and I shared, an experience that transformed us completely and altered the course of our lives,” she said in response. “This is the true story of our journey.”

She also called the investigation “grotesquely unfair” and shared photographs of redacted clinic letters, addressed to her husband, that appear to show that he was “treated for CBD/S [corticobasal syndrome] and has been for many years”.

The film was originally set to be released in the US and Canada on 22 May, but has been pushed back to 4 September. It’s being distributed by Rialto, whose CEO, Kelly Rogers, described the project as “a film of quiet power” and said that it “speaks to something deeply human”, according to Variety.

The film was a box office hit in the UK, where it earned £7.6m, making it one of 2025’s most successful British indie movies.

When the Salt Path scandal broke last summer, the book’s publisher, Penguin, said that it “undertook all the necessary due diligence” before releasing the book in 2018, and said that it had “not received any concerns about the book’s content” before the investigation was released.

Winn had been due to release another book, her fourth non-fiction title, On Winter Hill, in October 2025, but its publication has since been delayed to January 2028 after the author suffered “considerable distress”.

News.title: Shirtless Mark Zuckerberg spars with UFC champion in middle of lake
News.content:
Mark Zuckerberg sparred with UFC champion Merab Dvalishvili on board a floating barge in a lake, a video posted to Instagram on Sunday (9 August) shows.

The Facebook founder and Meta CEO was shirtless and barefoot as the pair exchanged kicks and punches.

"Merab made me take my shirt off because it looks more 'fighter,'" Zuckerberg told his wife, Priscilla Chan, who was canoeing nearby.

The session ended with the pair throwing each other off the floating platform into the water.

Zuckerberg is a known UFC fan and has previously trained with champions Israel Adesanya and Alexander Volkanovski on a speedboat.

A British Airways flight attendant has been praised after a viral video captured her threatening to restrain a disorderly passenger at Heathrow airport.

A TikTok posted by DJ and musician Bou, who said he was on flight BA275 to Las Vegas at the time, appears to show a man being separated by a female flight attendant from two other men.

Visibly angry, the man appears to be trying to reach over and grab the other men, pointing at them and shouting.

Meanwhile, the flight attendant in the middle shouts at the man to “stay seated” and “sit down”, while other cabin crew attempt to quell the disruption.

“I will be restraining you, sir, if you don’t stay seated,” the female flight attendant is heard saying in the video.

Bou, who was sitting in a higher class section of the plane, said in a clip that he could hear the disruption from his seat.

The musician said the video of the altercation was captured by his tour manager, and that later the plane returned to the terminal to allow police officers to board the aircraft.

The DJ praised the flight attendant and called on British Airways to give her a raise. Bou is seen in the video sampling the “stay seated” audio from the cabin crew member and turning it into a dance tune.

Bou, who was due to play a DJ set in Las Vegas, later invited the flight attendant along to his gig and played the remix while she danced on stage.

Comments under the video applauded the attendant, calling her a “legend” and joining in the calls for her pay rise.

The Metropolitan Police confirmed they were called out to Heathrow airport at around 5.30pm on Thursday, 6 August “following reports of a passenger being disruptive on an outbound plane.”

The person they escorted from the plane was later “charged with being drunk on an aircraft and disobeying the orders of the captain”.

Data from FlightRadar shows that the BA275 flight that day was due to take off at 5.15pm, but did not leave for Las Vegas until almost 8.30pm.

A spokesperson for British Airways told The Independent: "Disruptive or abusive behaviour is never tolerated on board and the safety of our customers and crew is our highest priority.

“When these incidents occur, the appropriate action will always be taken."
