World.title: ECZ engages political party agents, monitors in Masaiti
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) in Masaiti District has held meetings with political party agents, monitors and polling agents in Kafulafuta, Kalulalango and Masaiti Constituencies.

Speaking during the closing of the meetings, Masaiti Constituency Presiding Officer Lubombela Mulala urged polling agents and monitors to adhere to the Electoral Code of Conduct during and after polling day.

Mr Mulala said all stakeholders have a duty to contribute towards the attainment of free, fair and credible elections.

He said the meetings were aimed at acquainting polling agents and monitors with their roles and responsibilities, as well as encouraging them to remain vigilant and ensure peace is maintained through factual reporting.

Mr Mulala reminded the gathering that ECZ has not changed anything but is merely applying constitutional provisions governing the holding of General Elections.

He further reminded all aspiring candidates that they are required to provide two polling agents at every polling station, although only one agent is allowed inside the polling station at a time.

Mr Mulala also advised all participants in the elections to adhere to the lawful requirement to remove campaign posters and other campaign materials from walls, trees and other places within fourteen days after polling day.

He said it was important for polling agents and monitors to understand their roles and those of other stakeholders who will be visiting and operating from polling stations on polling day.

And one of the polling agents, Mr Zulu, commended ECZ for equipping them with knowledge on the roles and responsibilities of polling agents and monitors.

Mr Zulu said the information had come at an opportune time and would help polling agents conduct themselves professionally and foster peaceful elections.

World.title: Low Stakeholder Accreditation Worries ECZ In Vubwi
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has raised concern over the low turnout of stakeholders seeking accreditation to monitor and observe the August 13 general elections in Vubwi district.

Vubwi District Electoral Officer, Moses Mutyoka, said the number of political parties, Independent Candidates and other stakeholders obtaining accreditation remained low as of Saturday, August 8, with most participating political players having accredited only two members of staff.

The accreditation exercise is scheduled to close on Tuesday, August 11, 2026.

Professor Mutyoka urged political parties and other stakeholders to take the accreditation exercise seriously, warning that failure to obtain the necessary accreditation will result in polling agents being denied access to monitor the electoral process on polling day.

“Political parties are supposed to be at the forefront of acquiring accreditation. If you do not do so, your polling agents will not be allowed to monitor the elections. Make sure you do the needful,” he said.

He assured stakeholders that the ECZ was working throughout the accreditation period to ensure that all eligible persons were accredited, but encouraged them not to wait until the last minute.

Professor Mutyoka warned that late applications could result in unnecessary panic and congestion, potentially leaving some stakeholders unable to obtain the required accreditation documents before the deadline.

He further cautioned stakeholders that those who failed to take advantage of the opportunity to comply with the electoral procedures would have themselves to blame, as the Commission had provided adequate information on the requirements and procedures governing the elections.

The District Electoral Officer said the Commission remained committed to ensuring that the electoral process is transparent and credible, stressing that political parties have an important role to play in monitoring the polls.

He described the participation of political parties and other accredited stakeholders in monitoring the electoral process as an important component of a democratic election.

Professor Mutyoka also urged voters to safeguard their National Registration Cards (NRCs) and voters’ cards, which are required for them to cast their ballots.

He cautioned voters against surrendering their documents to other people, saying voters should remain in possession of their NRCs and voters’ cards at all times.

“The election day is fast approaching. Let us all protect and secure our votes by safeguarding and remaining in possession of our NRCs and voters’ cards. Do not allow anyone to mislead you or take possession of your documents. You cannot vote without these two important documents,” he advised.

Vubwi District, a rural district bordering Malawi and Mozambique, has 33,230 registered voters and 43 polling stations spread across all nine wards.

The district has so far recorded no cases of electoral violence, a development that is contributing to expectations of a peaceful, free and fair election.

World.title: Zalomius cautions against unverified information
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has cautioned civil society organisations, faith-based organisations, the media and, local and international election observers against sharing unverified information on social media, ahead of the August 13, 2026 general elections.

ECZ Chairperson Mwangala Zaloumis says stakeholders have an important role to play in promoting responsible access to information and maintaining public confidence in the electoral process.

ZANIS reports that Ms Zaloumis says stakeholders should rely on verified and authoritative information and seek clarification from the Commission through appropriate channels whenever concerns arise.

The ECZ Chairperson was speaking in Lusaka today when she updated and addressed local and international election observers and other stakeholders on the preparedness of the Commission to handle the polls.

She added that information gathered during election monitoring should be handled responsibly, accurately and within the appropriate context.

Ms Zaloumis has also urged stakeholders to distinguish between verified observations, allegations and speculation, and ensure that their reports and assessments are evidence-based, objective and fair.

The Chairperson stressed that the ECZ remains committed to conducting elections that are free, fair, transparent and credible, guided by the principles of impartiality, professionalism, accountability, transparency and inclusiveness.

Ms Zalomius said with only a few days remaining until polling day, all stakeholders have a responsibility to contribute to a peaceful, transparent and credible electoral process.

She has since urged stakeholders to ensure that Zambians are able to exercise their democratic right to vote peacefully and confidently on August 13, 2026.

Meanwhile, ECZ Voter Education Manager Emmah Mwiinga disclosed that 8,786,300 voters are registered on its register, urging them to effectively participate in this year’s polls.

In her presentation, the Voter Education Manager further said the Commission will dispatch 81,000 poll staff in the 13, 539 polling stations dotted across the country.

On the delimitation exercise, Ms Mwiinga said the Commission increased the number of constituencies from 156 to 226 following constitutional reforms necessitated by the Constitution Amendment Act Number 13 of 2025, which led to the delimitation of constituencies.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 11, 2026
World.content:
Zambia Election Set for Closely Fought Opposition Battle

Zambia's 13 August election has become a closely contested battle between the ruling United Party for National Development and the Tonse-Pamodzi opposition alliance, led by newcomer Brian Mundubile and backed by former Patriotic Front structures. The election is expected to test the opposition's strength and serve as a referendum on President Hakainde Hichilema's record. The government has made progress on debt restructuring, economic growth and inflation. But the high cost of living remains a big concern for voters. The poll is also taking place amid concerns over alleged state interference, restrictions on opposition activity and controversial legislative changes, making it a key test for Zambia's democracy.

WHO Warns DR Congo Ebola Response Falling Behind

More than 1,900 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak. 60-70% of deaths occur in communities before patients reach treatment centres. The WHO said that the concentration of healthcare services in Bunia, Ituri province, is forcing patients to travel long distances and seek care too late. Poor transport systems may also increase transmission. The agency plans to expand treatment facilities closer to communities, add 400 Ebola beds and strengthen public awareness and early referrals. WHO is also looking to the town of Aru, where no new cases have been reported for two weeks after authorities expanded surveillance and response beyond individual patients to surrounding communities.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Nigeria Lassa Fever Cases Reach 1,000 in 2026

Nigeria has reported 1,000 confirmed cases of Lassa fever and 237 deaths in 2026, with cases reported in 23 states and 116 local government areas. Five states, Ondo, Bauchi, Taraba, Edo and Benue, account for 86% of confirmed cases. At least 53 healthcare workers have also been infected, prompting the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention to introduce a 30-day protection plan for frontline staff. The agency has said that late presentation, high treatment costs, poor sanitation and limited awareness are contributing to the outbreak and high fatality rate. Lassa fever is a viral haemorrhagic disease transmitted primarily through contact with food or household items contaminated by the urine or faeces of infected rodents.

Malawi Land Audit Flags Irregular Plot Allocations

Malawi's Ministry of Lands is set to release findings from a pilot land ownership audit in Lilongwe that reportedly uncovered irregularities in the allocation of plots in the affluent Area 3 and Area 10. The audit was launched in February 2026 to improve transparency and accountability in land administration. It is said to have identified politically exposed individuals, including current and former ministers, judges and MPs, among those allegedly linked to irregular land acquisitions. The findings could trigger political controversy, with questions remaining over whether those implicated will be publicly named or face legal or disciplinary action.

UN Somalia Auction Raises Security Concerns

The UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) has opened a tender to auction vehicles, generators, IT equipment, medical supplies, construction machinery and other assets. This comes as Washington moves to end funding for the mission's logistical support by the end of 2026. UNSOS provides critical transport, fuel, food and other supplies to about 12,000 African troops and police serving under AUSSOM in the fight against al-Shabab. The auction has raised concerns among civil society groups over transparency and oversight. Regional leaders have warned that any premature reduction in international support could create a security vacuum as al-Shabab continues to operate in parts of Somalia.

Close 

Climate Change Shifts Africa's Malaria Risk

Climate change is reshaping malaria risk across Africa, with rising temperatures making parts of southern Africa and high-elevation areas of East Africa increasingly suitable for transmission, according to a new Nature study. Some parts of West and Central Africa may have become too hot for optimal malaria transmission. The region still bears about 95% of the global malaria burden. But experts warn that climate change is only part of the equation, with funding gaps, drug and insecticide resistance, and weak health systems still major threats. They are urging countries in emerging risk areas to step up malaria prevention and surveillance while maintaining elimination efforts in high-burden areas.

World.title: South Africa: Gauteng Gets 500,000 Grade 1 and 8 Applications - South African News Briefs - August 11, 2026
World.content:
Gauteng Records Nearly 500,000 Grade 1 and 8 Applications

Almost half a million applications have been submitted for Grade 1 and Grade 8 places in Gauteng for the 2027 academic year since the online application system opened, reports EWN. The Gauteng Department of Education has said that improvements have been made to streamline the process. Education MEC Lebogang Maile has urged parents to apply early. The department also says learners awaiting specialised placement should receive interim support rather than remain on waiting lists, with officials focusing on successful placements and resolving outstanding cases.

Strong Winds Damage Homes in Free State

The South African Red Cross Society is assessing damage caused by strong winds and heavy rainfall in Koppies and other parts of the Free State, reports SABC News. Several homes have reportedly been damaged, including roofs blown off, as severe weather persists. Red Cross volunteers are working with disaster management authorities and municipalities. Assessments continue, with humanitarian assistance being provided to affected households.

Fadiel Adams Unlikely to Testify at Madlanga Commission

National Coloured Congress leader Fadiel Adams is unlikely to testify before the Madlanga Commission, reports EWN. This comes after the commission received his affidavit and supporting documents late. Adams was expected to testify about his involvement in an Investigating Directorate Against Corruption probe into alleged corruption within Crime Intelligence. World.title: South Africa: Immigrant Traders See Their Livelihoods Destroyed By March and March
World.content:
Traders with documents and permits chased away, leaving Bellville bus terminus market almost empty

Dozens of immigrant traders who usually traded at the Golden Arrow terminus in Bellville are staying away because of anti-immigrant protests.

When we visited the once bustling site last week, it was quiet with only a handful of traders. Many stalls were deserted.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Some traders we spoke to said they had tried to set up shop in other areas but were stopped. They have not traded at the bus site since the March and March 30 June "deadline" demanding "illegal immigrants" leave South Africa.

"I need to pay rent, put food on the table, and pay the bills," a Zimbabwean man who asked to remain anonymous told GroundUp.

He said he has been selling clothes in Bellville for about five years. He left Zimbabwe in 2008 when its economy collapsed.

While he has not been directly threatened, he has witnessed others being harassed.

"They will take your stuff and throw it on the ground," he said.

"It hurts, but as much as it hurts, it's their country, and they're also marginalised people."

Another trader, who introduced herself as Meye, said she has had a permit to trade since 2010. She fled the DRC in 2003.

"We are legal; everything is correct. But they say we are foreigners and we need to go back to our country."

A single mother of three, she says she is now struggling to feed and school her children.

Another single mother, Safia, says she has been unable to trade despite having refugee status and a trading permit. She came from Somalia in 2010.

She said law enforcement needs to protect the traders better.

"I can't sleep at night because of what is happening. I can't even pay my rent. I can't support my children," she said.

Abdulhakim Husein, Western Cape director of the Somalia Association of South Africa, told GroundUp that he had been assisting traders since the start of July.

He said many asylum seekers and refugees are traders as they have to rely on being self-employed. They came from Somalia, DRC, Zimbabwe, Angola and Burundi.

He said that at a meeting on 13 July (which the City confirmed), it was agreed that traders with valid permits should be allowed to trade. But on 14 July, they received a message warning them about a March and March protest in the area.

Close 

Husein said they have approached a legal NGO for assistance.

City spokesperson Luthando Tyhalibongo said foreign nationals whose immigration status has been verified by Home Affairs are permitted to trade with a valid permit. These cost R78 per month.

"It is a concern whenever permitted traders, whether South African citizens or foreign nationals lawfully permitted to trade, are prevented from engaging in legal economic activity," he said.

He said intimidation and threats should be reported to SAPS.

World.title: Somalia: UN Puts Somalia Mission Assets Up for Sale As U.S. Funding Cutoff Looms
World.content:
Mogadishu, Somalia — The United Nations Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) has opened a tender seeking licensed auctioneers to sell off a wide range of its vehicles, generators and other equipment in Somalia, a notice published on the UN Global Marketplace shows.

The call for expressions of interest, issued August 6, comes as Washington moves to cut off funding for the UN's logistical support mission by the end of 2026, deepening uncertainty over the future of international backing for Somalia's fight against al-Shabab.

The tender matters now because it lands at the center of a widening rift between the United States and the United Nations over how and whether, to keep supporting Somalia's security transition. UNSOS underpins the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), supplying transport, fuel, food and other non-lethal supplies to roughly 12,000 African troops and police fighting a resilient insurgency. Any wind-down of that support network would strike at the core of the mission's ability to operate.

Under the terms of the tender, UNSOS is looking to establish a local contract for the "commercial sale" of UN-owned property. The initial deal would run three months, with up to three additional three-month extensions depending on performance and operational need.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The list of items up for sale is extensive: vehicles, generators, computers and IT equipment, office equipment, shipping containers, security watchtowers, wastewater treatment plants, prefabricated accommodation materials, medical and laboratory equipment, electrical appliances and heavy construction machinery. UNSOS said the list is indicative and may grow.

Interested firms have a narrow window to respond, with registration required by August 11 -- just five days after the notice was published.

Civil society analysts in Mogadishu have indicated that the auction notice does not lay out a clear mechanism for independent oversight, warning that disposing of mission assets without transparency could weaken public trust and open the door to diversion of state property.

The auction notice does not link the sale to the funding dispute. But it follows a July 1 letter in which the United States cited concerns over Somalia's performance against al-Shabab and its handling of security and governance issues, and comes as Washington has pushed back against extending UN logistical support for AUSSOM beyond current arrangements.

Somalia has fought al-Shabab for nearly two decades, and the group still holds sway over parts of the country. Leaders of AUSSOM troop-contributing nations have warned that a premature drawdown in support could open a security vacuum.

World.title: Malawi: Bombshell Land Audit to Name Ministers, Judges and MPs Over Illegal Plot Grabs
World.content:
Malawi's Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development is set to hold a highly anticipated press briefing this Wednesday to unveil the findings of a pilot land ownership audit conducted in Lilongwe - findings that are set to implicate some of the country's most powerful figures.

According to an invitation letter seen by this publication, Minister of Lands Chimwemwe Chipungu will personally preside over the briefing, which is expected to shed light on widespread irregularities uncovered during the audit process.

'The Ministry embarked on the Land Ownership Audit exercise in February 2026 as part of efforts to strengthen land administration systems, promote accountability in land ownership and enhance transparency and efficiency in the management of land resources,' the invitation reads.

The audit is understood to have uncovered significant irregularities in the allocation of plots specifically within Lilongwe's Area 3 and Area 10, two of the capital's most sought-after and valuable residential districts.



Most explosively, the audit has reportedly named a string of politically exposed individuals - including ministers serving in both the current and former administrations, sitting judges, and members of parliament - among those alleged to have acquired plots in the affected areas without following proper procedure.

The revelations, if confirmed at Wednesday's briefing, threaten to ignite a fresh political storm in Malawi, given the seniority of those reportedly implicated and the sensitivity surrounding land allocation in a country where access to prime urban plots has long been a source of controversy and allegations of favouritism.

The findings also land amid a period of intense scrutiny over transparency and accountability in public institutions more broadly, following separate controversies including the stalled parliamentary probe into the K128 billion Amaryllis Hotel purchase and mounting pressure over undisclosed presidential travel costs.

It remains to be seen whether Wednesday's briefing will name the individuals implicated publicly, or whether further legal or disciplinary action is being considered against those found to have benefited from irregular land allocations.

Ministry officials have not yet responded to requests for further comment ahead of the scheduled press briefing.

World.title: Uganda: Govt Orders Bus Drivers to Switch After Long Journeys to Curb Fatigue
World.content:
The government has introduced new measures requiring bus operators to change drivers after long-distance journeys, as authorities intensify efforts to curb driver fatigue following a series of fatal road crashes in recent weeks.

Works and Transport Minister Fred Byamukama announced the measures after meeting bus operators, Traffic Police and other transport stakeholders at the Ministry headquarters on Monday evening.

Under the new directive, buses travelling more than 300 kilometres will be required to have a different driver for the return journey.

A driver who completes the outbound journey on a route exceeding 300 kilometres will not be allowed to drive the same bus back along that route.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Traffic Police has been directed to apprehend operators and drivers who disregard the requirement.

For journeys of less than 300 kilometres, a driver will be allowed to travel to the destination and return once. After completing the return journey, the driver must stop work for the day and cannot undertake a third leg on the same day.

The measures are intended to reduce driver fatigue, which authorities and transport sector stakeholders have identified as one of the factors contributing to road crashes.

The directive comes after a series of deadly crashes involving buses and other passenger vehicles in July and early August.

On July 7, at least 14 people were killed and 28 injured when an Opit Travellers bus collided with a trailer at Bobi Trading Centre along the Kampala-Gulu Highway in Omoro District. Preliminary police findings linked the crash to reckless driving.

A week later, a bus carrying more than 70 students of Mwebaza High School to Jinja for a study trip collided with a passenger train at the Namumira railway crossing in Mukono. One teacher was killed and several students were injured.

The same week, another school bus carrying students from St Paul Secondary School, Katakwi, was involved in a crash along the Mbale-Iganga Highway after it rammed into a stationary trailer. The driver was killed and 15 people, most of them students, were injured.

The most serious incident occurred on July 16 when a King David Junior School bus carrying pupils from an educational trip to Sipi Falls crashed at Chekwatit along the Kapchorwa-Mbale Road.

Police subsequently confirmed that 24 people, including the bus driver, had died. Investigations into the cause of the crash remain ongoing.

The tragedy prompted the Ministry of Education and Sports to suspend all school trips and excursions. Police later clarified that the suspension applied to vehicles transporting learners on school trips and did not affect ordinary public transport buses.

The concentration of crashes involving buses and other passenger vehicles has also triggered calls for tougher enforcement of driver and vehicle safety requirements.

Transport leaders in Northern Uganda recently attributed the rising crashes to factors including driver fatigue, speeding, dangerous overtaking and indiscipline. They also urged bus companies to strengthen driver recruitment, check drivers' accident histories and ensure they receive adequate rest.

The Ministry of Works and Transport has separately proposed an electronic clocking-in system for public-service vehicle drivers to monitor their driving hours, rest periods and speeding.

The proposal was presented to Parliament's Committee on Physical Infrastructure in July after ministry officials reviewed a series of crashes.

The ministry said investigations into the July crashes had revealed non-compliance with transport regulations, including unlicensed buses, unaccredited drivers, mechanical defects and weak enforcement.

Under the proposed electronic monitoring system, drivers would record their journeys at designated points, allowing authorities to establish how long they had been driving and how much rest they had received.

The government has also said it plans to strengthen digital verification systems for detecting unlicensed vehicles and unauthorised drivers, while reviewing the National Road Safety Action Plan.

The recent measures build on earlier action against bus operators.

In May, the Ministry of Works and Transport suspended Nile Star bus operations for 30 days following a fatal crash in Nwoya in which seven passengers were killed and 16 others seriously injured.

The ministry said Nile Star buses had been involved in 11 crashes over the preceding year, resulting in 91 deaths and 56 injuries. The minister at the time cited possible driver fatigue and poor management of driver schedules among the concerns.

The government has also intensified scrutiny of heavy commercial vehicles. Earlier this month, authorities ordered all Sino trucks to undergo mandatory mechanical inspections within a two-month period, warning that vehicles failing to meet safety requirements could be taken off the road.

Close 

The renewed focus on bus operations comes as road crashes continue to claim lives.

On August 4, at least 14 people were killed when a passenger van collided with a sand-carrying truck in Kalungu District, according to police. Four others were injured, while the truck driver reportedly fled the scene.

Byamukama has urged bus operators to comply with the latest driver-management requirements, saying the measures are aimed at protecting passengers and other road users.

The government says Traffic Police will be expected to enforce the new rules, particularly on long-distance routes where driver fatigue can become a major safety risk.

The latest directive therefore adds another layer to the government's emerging road-safety strategy, which now includes tighter driver monitoring, scrutiny of vehicle condition, enforcement against unlicensed operators, restrictions on school transport activities and measures aimed at ensuring drivers get adequate rest.

ICE LINES UP TO BOOT ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHILD SEX PREDATOR AFTER BOGUS ASYLUM CLAIM, EARLY PRISON RELEASE

World.title: Florida woman accused of faking cancer to scam hundreds out of $40K, police say
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A Florida woman was arrested after authorities said she falsely claimed to have cancer and scammed more than 200 people out of more than $40,000 to pay off personal debts.

Maribeth Ellen Jones, 51, of Bonita Springs, has been charged with grand theft between $20,000 and $100,000. She turned herself in at the Naples Jail Center this week after detectives obtained a warrant for her arrest on the second-degree felony charge, according to the Collier County Sheriff’s Office.

Jones, who worked as an activities director in the community, allegedly told residents between 2022 and 2024 that she had cancer and was undergoing treatment, leading more than 200 people to donate to her because they believed she needed help.

OHIO BROTHERS WHO POSED AS MIDDLE EASTERN ROYALTY RECEIVE LENGTHY SENTENCE FOR $21M FRAUD SCHEME

Detectives said she even pretended her condition was worsening and had community members cut her hair to make it appear she was preparing to undergo chemotherapy.

Community members created a GoFundMe page for Jones that was linked to her personal bank account, according to the sheriff's office. They also gave her cash and personal checks.

WHAT SCAMMERS DO THE WEEK YOUR SPOUSE DIES

Jones had been the beneficiary of two previous GoFundMe campaigns in which she also claimed to have cancer, the sheriff's office said.

"GoFundMe has zero tolerance for the misuse of our platform and anyone who seeks to take advantage of the generosity of others," a GoFundMe spokesperson told Fox 13.

"We can confirm fundraisers organized on behalf of Maribeth Jones were removed from our platform, and her account was banned for any future fundraising. More than $41,000 was refunded to donors on the platform through GoFundMe’s Giving Guarantee, which offers a full refund in the rare case something isn’t right," the spokesperson continued.

Detectives said their investigation determined Jones did not have cancer and that she used the donated money to pay personal debts.

She is accused of defrauding 238 Naples residents out of more than $40,000.

"This is an appalling case because it exploited the kindness and generosity of people who truly wanted to help someone they believed was fighting for her life," Sheriff Kevin Rambosk said in a statement. "If you lie to steal from the generosity of others in Collier County, we will arrest you and hold you accountable."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"This type of scam not only hurts victims financially, it undermines trust in legitimate fundraisers for people who genuinely need help," Rambosk added.

World.title: President Trump warns FIFA will pay a massive price if it ousts chief Gianni Infantino
World.content:
President Donald Trump is handing out a big red card to FIFA’s bosses, warning soccer’s top execs they’d be out of their minds to dump embattled president Gianni Infantino.

Taking to Truth Social, Trump went to bat for Infantino, who faces an all-out revolt from global soccer leaders after a disastrous scheme to sell off a chunk of the men’s World Cup to private equity investors.

"FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino," Trump posted.

TRUMP ADMIN TAUNTS LEFT FOR ‘PRAYING’ FOR WORLD CUP DISASTER AS DOT TOUTS RECORD NUMBERS

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!"

Trump has is on the money concerning, well, the money.

The 2026 World Cup across America was a total monster as it packed stadiums and smashed revenue records. Say what you want, but nobody puts on a sports spectacle quite like the USA.

Yet the president's defense comes as Infantino’s internal trouble reaches a boiling point.

EUROPEAN SOCCER'S GOVERNING BODY FLIPS SPORT UPSIDE DOWN WITH BOYCOTT OF FIFA, FUTURE WORLD CUPS

The Swiss-Italian soccer boss ignited a firestorm by proposing a commercial entity dubbed FIFA Forward Enterprise, which would sell private investors a 20% stake in World Cup commercial rights for a $4.2 billion payday.

For that, Infantino got slammed.

Soccer's power brokers wanted no part of it. Leaders across Europe, Asia and North America rejected the deal, accusing Infantino of trying to quietly sell off the sport's crown jewels. He quickly scrapped the proposal and apologized, but the revolt was already rolling.

UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF then unloaded on the FIFA boss, accusing him of deception and abandoning his duty. European leaders have even floated a boycott of FIFA events, while execs behind closed doors are plotting rival tournaments that could leave Infantino on the outside looking in before the next election cycle.

FIFA REPORTEDLY WILLING TO LET TRUMP HAND WORLD CUP TROPHY TO WINNING CAPTAIN AT METLIFE STADIUM

Then there’s the Trump factor.

Could Infantino’s close relationship with the president be adding even more fuel to the revolt?

Trump, who was firmly in Infantino’s corner throughout the World Cup, clearly sees the fight through a dollars-and-cents lens.

Whether Infantino survives the red cards flying from every direction remains to be seen.

But Trump has picked his side — and he’s warning FIFA that dumping Infantino could come with one hell of a price tag.

World.title: DiJonai Carrington, who declared 'White privilege' after ejection, plays vs Storm as WNBA remains silent
World.content:
The WNBA's silence regarding DiJonai Carrington, who declared "White privilege" after her ejection during Saturday’s game against the Indiana Fever after smacking Sophie Cunningham in the face, meant she could play Monday night for the Chicago Sky against the Seattle Storm.

With the league not announcing any discipline for the veteran guard after her Flagrant 2 foul against the Fever over the weekend, Carrington checked into the game with 5:21 left in the first quarter.

There was a loud cheer coming from the Storm crowd, but it's unknown if it was because Carrington was checking into the game, or if they were cheering on rookie center Awa Fam entering for Seattle.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

With around two minutes left in the first quarter of Saturday’s 90-86 win for the Fever, Cunningham had a breakaway toward the hoop with Carrington trying to track her down to avoid an easy two points for Indiana.

Carrington’s hustle led to a meeting at the rim, but instead of swatting the ball, she hit Cunningham hard in the face, sending her to the floor as officials quickly blew the whistle.

DIJONAI CARRINGTON DECLARES ‘WHITE PRIVILEGE’ AFTER EJECTION FOR SMACKING SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM IN THE FACE

Cunningham was livid, getting up from the hardwood and confronting Carrington face-to-face. As she was being held back by teammates, she shoved Carrington slightly before officials stepped in as well.

After official review, Carrington’s foul was upgraded to a Flagrant 2, and she was ejected from the game.

Shortly after, and presumably from the locker room, Carrington posted on her Threads account, "WHITE PRIVILEGE," while tagging the Fever team account. She didn't initially elaborate on why she posted that, leaving it unclear whether she was referring to Cunningham, the official’s decision to deem the foul a Flagrant 2, or the Fever organization. Carrington didn’t accuse Cunningham by name, and there was no evidence that the foul was connected to Cunningham’s position on transgender athletes in women’s sports, which has been a hot-button WNBA topic in recent weeks.

On Monday, though, Carrington replied on X to a segment by ex-NFL player and sports personality Emmanuel Acho, who criticized the Sky player for calling the foul "White privilege."

"I've never once claimed that the assessment of the foul was white privilege (that was your assumption). Try exercising your critical thinking skills, I know you studied psych," Carrington's reply read on X. "Furthermore, I'm the LAST thing from ignorant or asinine when it comes to speaking on "white privilege," do ya research on that one. I actually went to school, one of the top universities might I add, to educate myself on this exact subject. I would never use that term as a rhetorical weapon knowing the historical and social weight it holds without having the proper evidence to substantiate it."

Cunningham has been at the center of a widening political debate about biological men in women’s sports, as supporters of her stance held a fourth rally outside the Fever road game at the United Center in Chicago on Saturday, while counter-protesters also gathered near the venue.

Cunningham has stated she does not harbor any hatred toward transgender people, but she believes protecting girls and women in sports is "common sense." She has received backlash for her belief, and the debate has spilled inside and outside of WNBA venues, while discourse continues online.

Meanwhile, this isn’t the first time Carrington has been at the center of controversy involving Fever players. During the 2024 campaign, where she was playing with the Connecticut Sun, Carrington mocked then-rookie Caitlin Clark for what she believed was flopping and later called Fever supporters "the nastiest fans in the W" after receiving racist abuse from online users.

Then, Carrington struck Clark in the eye while defending a pass during the 2024 WNBA Playoffs, leading to the latter having a black eye. Both players said that the contact was accidental, though Carrington drew some renewed criticism after she appeared to joke about the controversy during an Instagram Live video.

Carrington has also previously defended her style of play, which has been deemed dirty by some. She said she plays aggressively, but is always attempting to make a play on the ball.

CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP

Beyond basketball, she has drawn attention for wearing an explicit anti-President Donald Trump sweatshirt and urging WNBA players to oppose Trump administration policies affecting women and the LGBTQ community.

Carrington is in her sixth WNBA season, her first with the Sky, where she is averaging 9.8 points and 2.2 rebounds across her five games in a depth role for Chicago.

Fox News' Jackson Thompson and Matthew Reigle contributed to this report.

World.title: Trump used catering truck, Air Force One decoy to evade Iran threat: report
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

President Donald Trump secretly boarded a third, smaller U.S. military aircraft using an airport catering truck as cover to depart the NATO summit in Turkey in July while using an older Air Force One jet as a decoy, according to reports.

Citing an official and other material it reviewed, The Washington Post reported that the undercover maneuver took place at Ankara airport amid a credible Iranian threat against the president.

Trump had arrived in the Turkish capital on July 8 aboard a brand-new Boeing 747-8, an aircraft donated by Qatar.

Following U.S. military strikes against Iranian targets earlier in the summer, intelligence officials identified a specific threat from Iran targeting the president's movements.

TRUMP TAKES INAUGURAL FLIGHT ABOARD NEW AIR FORCE ONE AHEAD OF LIBRARY DEBUT HONORING FAMED OUTDOORSMAN

To counter the threat, U.S. security officials executed a ruse on the Turkish tarmac, according to the outlet.

Trump walked up the stairs of the legacy blue-and-white Boeing 747 — the older Air Force One — and waved to news cameras before entering the cabin.

Minutes later, Trump and a small team of aides were said to have stepped out of view into an airport catering truck that had been lifted to an exit door on the far side of the plane.

TRUMP SAYS HE'S IRAN'S 'NO. 1' TARGET AS RENEWED CONFLICT RAISES ASSASSINATION FEARS

The truck lowered to ground level and drove across the tarmac to a nearby Air Force C-32A, a modified Boeing 757.

Meanwhile, the media and White House staff boarded the older 747, believing Trump was inside.

Reporters were then instructed to close their window shades for takeoff, and the jet took off as a decoy, according to the Washington Post.

The legacy jet initially appeared on radar without a call sign before taking the ‘AF1’ call sign midflight, despite Trump not being aboard, according to flight-tracking data reviewed by the outlet.

Trump then flew in secrecy aboard the smaller C-32A to RAF Mildenhall in England, landing shortly before the decoy jet.

NEW AIR FORCE ONE TAKES FLIGHT AS TRUMP UNVEILS REVAMPED PRESIDENTIAL AIRCRAFT

It is unclear how Trump transferred from the C-32A to the legacy Air Force One after landing in the U.K.

At about 10:56 p.m., he appeared before TV cameras and descended the legacy aircraft’s external stairs, according to a media pool report.

Trump boarded the new Qatari-donated Boeing 747-8 for the return flight to Washington at about 11:01 p.m. Staff and reporters also transferred from the legacy aircraft before departing.

Reporters asked the president about why the window shades were ordered down in Turkey. Trump told them: "You're probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleaze bags that we have to deal with."

The president added that he faces threats constantly and is "Number One" on Iran's target list.

When reached by Fox News for comment on the Washington Post's reporting, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung said the new Air Force One is a "state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff."



He added: "As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The U.S. Air Force similarly touted the new Air Force One jet's safety.

"The aircraft is safe, secure and equipped with the most advanced technologies necessary to meet the requirements of the presidential mission," the Air Force said in a statement to Fox News. "Those requirements were carefully crafted to prioritize mission over aesthetics, leaving much of the previous head of state interior layout minimally changed. No risk was taken in security, safety or mission communications, but the collective team made trades on some of the less commonly used mission sets that Boeing must deliver to support the next 40 years."

Fox News also reached out to the U.S. Secret Service for comment.

Fox News' Pat Ward contributed to this report.

World.title: Fauci texts suggest officials were ‘too slow to pivot' amid pandemic, says Dr Marc Siegel
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Newly released text messages from Dr. Anthony Fauci have sparked fresh questions about his handling of evolving COVID-19 evidence, according to Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News senior medical analyst.

The texts are part of an initial batch of communications from Fauci's government-issued cellphone released Monday by Sens. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., and Rand Paul, R-Ky. The messages shed light on private discussions between Fauci and other top health officials as they navigated evolving questions around the coronavirus pandemic.

In a Monday evening interview, Siegel suggested the former White House chief medical adviser was at times too "dogmatic" and slow to adapt as the science evolved.

EXPOSED FAUCI DIARY SHOWS HE ESTIMATED COVID-19 DEATH RATE TO BE MUCH LOWER THAN WHAT HE TOLD CONGRESS

Siegel said Fauci was a "top immunologist" and "top vaccinologist."

"And I respect that a lot," he said, adding that he felt Fauci then ventured beyond those areas of expertise.

"The other issue is flexibility. I have a feeling about Dr. Fauci that he's too dogmatic," Siegel told Fox News Digital, adding that Fauci would "stick to some idea he has and [follow] it through regardless of contradictory or changing evidence."

Siegel said he believed Fauci veered into territory beyond his medical training and knowledge, on issues including lockdowns, school closures and masking.

LEGACY MEDIA COVERS ANTHONY FAUCI DIARY BY CRITICIZING DONALD TRUMP INSTEAD OF FAUCI'S DISHONESTY

"So it's not surprising that he would, for lack of a better word, flip-flop on those areas," he said.

Regarding the newly released texts, Siegel said "it looks like he was trying to guide other public officials and leaders from the television camera, and that's not what you should be doing."

Questions around pregnancy guidance

Among the issues addressed in the newly released messages is COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy.

Siegel emphasized that he remains a strong supporter of vaccines, including mRNA technology.

"I'm a big fan of the COVID vaccines and of the mRNA COVID vaccines," the doctor said. "I think they're getting a bad rap right now."

Pregnancy presented a complicated risk calculation because COVID-19 itself posed dangers to expectant mothers, Siegel noted.

Early in the pandemic, he said, recommending vaccination during pregnancy was reasonable based on what was known at the time.

But as the virus changed and vaccines became less protective, Siegel said he believes the public discussion should have changed with it.

CLICK HERE TO 

"As the vaccine changed and the virus mutated, and as the vaccine became less protective, that needed to be entered into the public debate about the vaccine — and Dr. Fauci wasn't fast enough to do that," Siegel said.

Siegel also pointed to a study that raised questions at the time about a potential link between a second vaccine dose and early miscarriage.

"I don't think that Dr. Fauci and others may have been quick enough to consider that," he said.

While subsequent research has continued to support vaccination during pregnancy — Siegel said "the accumulation of data right now favors the vaccine throughout pregnancy" — he questioned whether contradictory evidence received sufficient consideration as it emerged.

"It's a little eyebrow-raising to me that it appears he was trying to dismiss a study" suggesting miscarriage could be a concern, Siegel said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

More broadly, such decisions should rest with patients and their doctors, while emphasizing that the underlying medical data was "not suppressed," according to the doctor.

"I don't like when the government superimposes their views, especially if they're incorrect or if they are ill-informed, but I still think it should be between the patient and the doctor," said Siegel.

‘The mandates continued'

Siegel argued that another problem came when policies failed to adjust quickly enough to changing evidence about the vaccines' effectiveness.

"I think the problem was that the mandates continued," he said. "We were too slow to pivot on this vaccine, and that led to a lot of public distrust."

Asked whether he saw a meaningful difference between what Fauci was discussing privately and what Americans were hearing publicly, Siegel said there was "more than I would like."

"There's a difference between public and private discourse here," he said. "There should be none."

"Where was the evolution of guidance and thought and staying within your lane as more and more information came out?"

As additional messages are released, Siegel said he will be watching how Fauci's guidance evolved alongside the evidence.

"I'm looking at one thing: Where was the evolution of guidance and thought and staying within your lane as more and more information came out?" he said. "Or did this develop more and more into dogma and megalomania? I don't know. That's what I'm disturbed about."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

At the same time, Siegel cautioned against judging pandemic-era communications without considering what scientists knew at the time.

"To be fair to Dr. Fauci, things need to remain in context," he said. "When did this happen? What was going on at the time? What did we know and what did we not know?"

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Added Siegel, "We were learning on the job. We were learning as we went. We knew nothing about this thing, and it just blew over us."

That uncertainty, he said, made a willingness to change course all the more important.

"Humility is the best way to go — not dogma."

World.title: Quinnen Williams agrees to $105.9M contract extension with Cowboys, locking him in through 2030 season
World.content:

The Dallas Cowboys and veteran defensive tackle Quinnen Williams agreed to a three-year extension prior to the start of the 2026 NFL season that will make him one of the highest-paid players at his position.

Williams agreed to an extension worth $105.9 million, including $101 million in guaranteed money and $63.35 million guaranteed at signing. He is also getting a signing bonus worth $31.85 million.

Williams, who has made the last four Pro Bowls, was traded to the Cowboys before the deadline last season in a blockbuster deal with the New York Jets.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The Jets, who were in the middle of another lackluster season, decided to trade away Williams and cornerback Sauce Gardner (Indianapolis Colts), parting ways with two top four NFL Draft choices as they continue to rebuild.

Williams’ trade was interesting considering the Jets inked him to a four-year extension worth $96 million with $66 million guaranteed in 2023. The Jets acquired a second-round pick in 2026, a 2027 first-round pick and defensive tackle Mazi Smith in exchange for Williams.

DALLAS COWBOYS SET THEMSELVES UP FOR INTERNET MOCKERY WITH CALEB DOWNS TROPHY WALKTHROUGH

Now, the Cowboys have one of the best at the position locked in through the 2030 campaign – a priority that team executive vice president Stephen Jones mentioned at the start of training camp.

Williams became the fourth defensive tackle to sign a deal averaging more than $30 million per season, joining the Philadelphia Eagles’ Jalen Carter (four years, $152 million), Tennessee Titans’ Jeffery Simmons (three years, $105.8 million), and Kansas City Chiefs’ Chris Jones (five years, $158.75 million).

And the Cowboys have not been shy about flexing their finances, as fellow defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa was signed to a four-year, $80 million extension to remain a key piece on defense next to Williams.

With Kenny Clark, who was acquired in the Micah Parsons trade to the Green Bay Packers, and Rashan Gary, the former Packers defensive end who joined the team in free agency this offseason, also on board for the Cowboys, they have a revamped defense that can match the firepower their offense clearly showcased in Brian Schottenheimer’s first year as head coach in 2025.

In his seven games with Dallas last season, Williams tallied 21 combined tackles, 1.5 sacks, three tackles for loss and nine quarterback hits.

For his career, Williams has totaled 343 combined tackles – 62 for loss – 41.5 sacks, eight forced fumbles and earned a First Team All-Pro nod during his breakout 2022 campaign with the Jets, where he had 12 sacks.

World.title: RFK Jr. wants to fix loophole that allows additives into food. Critics say it doesn’t go far enough.
World.content:
The Trump administration said it’s taking first steps in strengthening rules over ingredients food companies have long added to their products with minimal oversight.

Under a proposed rule announced Monday, manufacturers will have to notify the Food and Drug Administration when they deem additives as “generally recognized as safe,” also known as GRAS, as well as provide information on existing additives.

But critics say that while this is a good first step, the proposed rule won’t prevent manufacturers from adding new ingredients to foods, nor will it remove the many thousands of additives already in foods.

The GRAS designation, which began in the 1950s, was meant to simplify the use of common ingredients like paprika, garlic and vanilla and avoid a lengthy approval process while also freeing up the FDA’s limited resources. Companies are not required to tell the FDA when deciding what they consider GRAS.

Critics, including public health experts and food scientists, have long said the industry has exploited the rule to introduce thousands of unstudied chemicals into the nation’s food supply, potentially endangering public health.

Deeming an ingredient GRAS does not necessarily make it so, and the FDA has banned certain ingredients from food after evidence emerged that they might harm health. These include Red No. 3, a synthetic dye that gives foods and drinks a bright cherry red color but has been linked to cancer in animals, and brominated vegetable oil, often used in citrus-flavored drinks, which has been linked to liver, heart and brain damage.

“Over time, that exemption has become the loophole, and the vast majority of substances have been submitted via that loophole without public disclosure or of the information safety,” Dr. Dariush Mozaffarian, director of the Food Is Medicine Institute at Tufts University, said during a media event Monday with Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

The proposed rule would require companies to notify the FDA when they deem substances as GRAS. The notices would be made public. For substances that already have GRAS designations, the proposed rule would ask companies to submit data about how those ingredients are used.

“The new rule does not prevent companies from self-affirming the safety of their ingredients,” said Alyssa Moran, deputy director of the Center for Food and Nutrition Policy at the University of Pennsylvania. “It does require mandatory notification, but my understanding is that there’s not even a timeline for notification, so companies can introduce these ingredients and then eventually notify FDA.”

Thousands of ingredients have been designated “generally recognized as safe” since the 1950s. Joe Raedle / Getty Images file

“It’s just quite misleading to say we’re going to close the GRAS loophole, and then to still allow companies to self-affirm the safety of their ingredients,” Moran added.

Jennifer Pomeranz, associate professor of public health policy and management at the New York University School of Global Public Health, said the proposed rule was “an incredibly important first step” but said more work is needed.

“What data is going to be required to be submitted about the ingredients already in the food supply?” Pomeranz said. “It has to be enough for us to see that it’s safe. It can’t just be a name of an ingredient and its uses.”

Stephanie Harris, chief public policy officer for the Food Industry Association, which represents grocers and other food suppliers, said that the GRAS proposal is “an important step” but shows limits of what the FDA can do to make such reforms, legally.

“Congress should act this year to establish a nationally uniform, science-based framework for ingredient transparency that strengthens FDA’s role, avoids a fragmented state-by-state patchwork and provides consumers and the food industry with clarity and confidence,” Harris said in a statement.

During the media event, Kennedy also announced a federally recognized definition for ultraprocessed foods is under “final review” but did not provide the text of the definition. A spokesperson for the Department of Health and Human Services did not give a timeline for when that would be made public.
