World.title: One year after Putin-Trump summit, ‘spirit of Anchorage’ dissipated
World.content:
Moscow – In the year since Donald Trump hosted Vladimir Putin on US soil for a summit designed to broker an end to Russia’s offensive on Ukraine, the diplomatic initiative has fizzled out and the conflict has escalated.

For months, Russian officials talked up the “spirit of Anchorage” — a supposed climate of detente, renewed dialogue with Washington and a framework for finding a way out of the deadliest European conflict since World War II.

Now there are few traces of that atmosphere. US mediation efforts are at a standstill, both Russia and Ukraine are ramping up attacks and more civilians are being killed than at any point since the first months of the war.

– ‘Ending the war’-

On August 15, 2025, Trump broke with the West’s policy of isolating Putin, rolling out the red carpet as the Kremlin chief stepped off his plane at the Elmendorf-Richardson air base in Alaska.

It remains unclear what was decided or discussed behind closed doors.

Russia has always maintained some kind of understanding on a peace deal was struck — “a compromise proposal”, as Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov called it.

Washington has rebuffed any talk of a deal being reached.

“There was a proposal in Alaska, but there was no agreement. If there had been an agreement, we would have had an end of the war,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in June.

Moscow had hoped the summit would lay the foundations for a “lasting peace” by addressing what it calls the “root causes” of the conflict, said political analyst Sergei Markov — designated a “foreign agent” but still close to the Russian authorities.

For years — including right before launching its offensive in February 2022 — Russia has called for a new overarching security deal with the United States over Europe, NATO and arms control.

The “compromise” Russia tabled in Alaska, Markov told AFP, was to limit its territorial claims on Ukraine to the eastern Donbas region in exchange for recognition of Russia’s new borders by Washington and the lifting of sanctions.

– Disenchantment –

Those Russian demands were included in a 28-point document drafted by the United States — later cut down to 19 — after separate negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow.

The document was never published officially and never came to fruition.

US-brokered direct talks between Russia and Ukraine in early 2026 broke down, chiefly over the issue of territory.

Ukraine refuses to cede land it still controls and wants an immediate ceasefire along the current front line, with territorial status to be decided during fuller peace talks.

And since late February, Washington’s attention has been consumed by the war on Iran.

Trump has since issued fresh sanctions on Russia and the last remaining nuclear arms control agreement — New Start — has been allowed to lapse.

Having once sensed a window of opportunity to press its demands and been at pains to praise Trump’s efforts, Russia has lately allowed itself to publicly question Washington’s commitment to diplomacy.

“I don’t even want to imagine that Alaska … was conceived to gain time in order to strengthen Ukraine militarily,” Lavrov said in June.

A meeting between Lavrov and Rubio in Manila in July — their first since September 2025 — lasted only around 30 minutes.

“We’ll have to find new suggestions and new ideas” that both “Russia and Ukraine can agree to,” Rubio said after that meeting.

“That’s going to require a lot of work,” he added.

– Escalation –

The two sides’ conditions for peace are irreconcilable.

Russia demands territory alongside political and military concessions that Ukraine rejects as capitulation.

At the same time, both are convinced force can improve their negotiating position.

“The Russian armed forces will continue their mission to liberate the Donbas and Novorossiya in line with the approved plan,” Russia’s army chief Valery Gerasimov told Putin in a televised meeting in early July — referring to land stretching across eastern and southern Ukraine.

Buoyed by European support, Kyiv is banking on its long-range strike campaign to tip Russia’s economy and society over the edge.

Its attacks triggered a nationwide fuel crisis over the summer, and have forced Moscow-installed authorities to put the annexed Crimean peninsula under a local “state of emergency”.

Russia has upped its missile attacks on Kyiv, killing dozens there in recent weeks.

It has also brought Ukrainian exports through the Black Sea to a standstill through a campaign of port and ship strikes.

“The spirit of Anchorage has dissipated,” said Russian political analyst Fyodor Lukyanov — close to the ruling elite — in August.

The result? “Brutal escalation.”

World.title: AI’s hunger for power sparks US private gas plant boom
World.content:
Washington – As US tech companies race to build the data centers fueling the AI boom, they are increasingly putting up their own power plants — off the grid and running on gas — to get online faster.

Analysis by the research firm Cleanview, shared with AFP, identified around 60 data centers planned for the coming years with a combined 97 gigawatts of “behind-the-meter” generation into the early 2030s — around the total installed capacity of Mexico.

The climate implications could be enormous.

The precise figure depends on how many are built, how efficient the turbines are and how often they run, but even with very conservative assumptions, the plants would easily top 200 million tons of carbon dioxide emissions a year.

That’s equal to annual emissions of more than 46 million gasoline-powered cars.

The latest addition to the tally — a 7.5 GW plant in Texas powering Amazon data centers — shows how analysts often have to piece together clues to link projects to hyperscalers.

The plant got air pollution permits in January, Amazon received construction permits last week, and satellite imagery confirmed clearing had begun at the site named in the plant’s air permit records. Cleanview then confirmed the link with Amazon directly.

– Poor efficiency –

Alongside greenhouse gases, gas plants emit fine particulate matter, linked to a range of heart and lung problems; nitrogen oxides, which aggravate respiratory disease; and hazardous air pollutants including mercury, formaldehyde and benzene.

“Powering data centers with behind-the-meter generation that relies heavily on dirty gas or diesel turbines is a surefire way to needlessly pump a variety of hazardous pollutants into local communities’ air while worsening climate change,” John Rogers, associate director of energy analytics at the Union of Concerned Scientists, told AFP.

“These dirty plants, which are also subject to less public accountability, are unacceptable when record heat and fires are showing us that we need to change course,” said Yuqi Zhu, a senior policy analyst at Natural Resources Defense Council.

The practice began as an oddity, exemplified by Elon Musk’s decision to truck in mobile gas turbines to an xAI data center in Memphis in 2024. xAI still accounts for most of the two gigawatts online today.

But Cleanview’s analysis finds nearly every hyperscaler is pursuing such projects, including Meta, Microsoft and Oracle. AI labs including OpenAI and Anthropic have signed leases for more than 10 gigawatts of behind-the-meter power.

Instead of the equipment utilities normally buy, they have turned to more exotic and more polluting options, including trailer-mounted generators, turbines originally designed for aircraft and warships, piston engines of the kind commonly found in vehicles, and refurbished turbines from industrial operations.

– Test case –

Development tilts toward Republican-leaning states, with Texas far in the lead at more than 40 gigawatts announced.

The NAACP civil rights group has filed suit against xAI, accusing it of unlawfully operating turbines in Mississippi to power its Memphis data center.

“We are concerned that if this case is decided against us, data centers across the country will be emboldened to go forward,” Laura Thoms, enforcement director at Earthjustice, which is co-representing the NAACP, told AFP.

President Donald Trump’s administration has created a voluntary “Ratepayer Protection Pledge,” under which signatories promise not to pass data center costs on to residential consumers, something Thoms fears will only accelerate the problem.

Gas was already enjoying a renaissance before Trump returned to office, according to data compiled by Atlas Public Policy.

After years of decline, new announced fossil fuel capacity for the grid hit a low in 2022, rebounding the following year as the AI boom took hold.

“In the first half of 2026 alone, we’re already seeing that the announced new (fossil) capacity is higher than it’s been in the last 10 years, so that’s a pretty significant sign,” said Rachel Reolfi, a senior policy analyst at the group.

World.title: Iraq unveils dual pipeline plan to Faysh Khabur and Baniyas via Chevron
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Monday, August 10, 2026, plans to construct a major new pipeline network featuring two strategic export routes toward Faysh Khabur and the Syrian port of Baniyas. The infrastructure push aims to diversify Iraq’s crude oil export outlets beyond its primary southern Gulf terminals.

Deputy Oil Minister for Extraction Affairs, Nseer Aziz, chaired an executive planning meeting to establish implementation frameworks for the multi-billion-dollar project. Discussions centered on finalizing investment mechanics under a Build-Own-Operate-Transfer (BOOT) model with a consortium of global energy firms including UCC, TI Capital, and Chevron.

Key Infrastructure & Project Details

Dual Export Corridors: Route 1:Basra – Haditha – Faysh Khabur (connecting southern oilfields to northern export infrastructure near the Turkish border). Route 2:Haditha – Baniyas (reactivating the strategic Mediterranean export route across Syria).

Investment Model: To be executed under a BOOT (Build-Own-Operate-Transfer) framework in partnership with international consortium partners Chevron, UCC, and TI Capital.

Inter-Agency Coordination: Attended by leadership from Basra Oil Company (BOC), North Oil Company (NOC), Missan Oil Company (MOC), state oil marketer SOMO, and the Ministry’s Studies and Planning Directorate.

Syrian Transit Agreement: Follows a U.S.-sponsored Memorandum of Understanding signed between Iraq and Syria on July 17, 2026, to reactivate the historic Kirkuk–Baniyas pipeline corridor.

The dual-pipeline initiative marks a decisive effort by Baghdad to reduce its reliance on southern Gulf ports following severe disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

By linking Basra’s southern production hubs directly to northern transit corridors at Faysh Khabur and Mediterranean terminals at Baniyas, Iraq aims to secure uninterrupted crude flows to global markets, lower war-risk freight costs, and enhance long-term energy marketing flexibility.

World.title: 'Zealots overlooked human nature': Shashi Tharoor questions full Vande Mataram rendition at official events
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress MP

on Tuesday questioned the practical implications of the Vande Mataram amendment, saying the requirement to sing the National Song in full at official functions could result in audiences standing for several minutes before and after events.

In a post on X, Tharoor said the President had assented to the amendment, which was passed in Parliament without discussion. He said the amended provision requires the full National Song to be sung at the beginning and end of official functions, in addition to the

.

"The President has assented to the #VandeMataram Amendment, passed without discussion in Parliament, which requires the singing of the National Song in full at the start and ending of any official function, in addition to the National Anthem.

"As one who greatly respects both, and can sing the first two stanzas of the former (but not the other four, which were never required till now) as well as the entire anthem, i would like to point to just one practical consideration our zealots appear to have overlooked: human nature," Tharoor added.

He said, "'Jana Gana Mana' requires audiences to stand respectfully and focus their attention for a reasonable 52 seconds.





The National Song in full takes 3 minutes and 10 seconds. Tamil Nadu has just decided that both will be preceded by the State Song in Tamil for another 2 minutes. Do we really expect audiences to stand still and respectfully for six minutes before and after every function, a total of 12 extra minutes? Can respect and patience be legislated? I fear that the intent of the Bill, to promote greater respect for the National Song , will not be achieved, but its opposite may well be.

World.title: Dharmendra Pradhan calls Rahul Gandhi 'habitual liar', takes 'selective democracy' jibe at Congress
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Union education minister and senior

leader

on Tuesday trained his guns on Lok Sabha leader of opposition

, branding him a âhabitual liarâ and accusing the

Congress

of shedding âcrocodile tearsâ over studentsâ concerns.

Pradhanâs remarks came amid protests in Jharkhand over irregularities and paper leaks in competitive examinations. In Jharkhand, Congress is part of the ruling alliance with Jharkhand Mukti Morcha led by chief minister Hemant Soren in the state.

In a post on X, former Union education minister accused the Congress of âcontinuously spreading liesâ about studentsâ interests and alleged that Rahul Gandhi âlacks factsâ.

âThe leader of opposition, who habitually lies, neither wants to come to Parliament nor listen to answers. They just want to spread their lies and shed crocodile tears,â Pradhan said.

Pradhan also hit back at the oppositionâs sustained attack on the Centre and Union home minister Amit Shah, accusing Rahul Gandhi and the Congress of making âbaselessâ and âfactlessâ allegations.

âMaking baseless, factless false accusations against the Honorable Home Minister Shri Amit Shah ji reveals the political desperation of Rahul Gandhi and the Congress,â Sambalpur MP said.





The former Union minister also maintained that the government was ready for a discussion in Parliament on âevery issueâ, while accusing the Congress of deliberately disrupting proceedings.

âThe government is ready for discussion in Parliament on every issue, but Congress is obstructing the temple of democracy, Parliament House, and crushing the interests of the country and the youth,â he said.

Pradhan alleged that the oppositionâs objective was political, rather than addressing issues concerning the country and young people.

He also accused Congress leaders of creating âchaosâ outside Parliament when discussions are held inside the House.

Turning the spotlight on the JMM-Congress government in Jharkhand, Pradhan accused it of following a policy of âselective democracyâ over the handling of student protests.

âCongressâs democracy is also âselectiveâ-violence against youth where they are in government, and lies and commotion where they want to shine politically,â he said, referring to the use of lathi-charge, water cannons and tear gas against protesting students in Jharkhand.

Pradhan also questioned Lok Sabha LoP Rahul's silence on the Jharkhand protests, saying the Congress leader holds press conferences on âevery issueâ but has not spoken about the student agitation. Meanwhile, Rahul held a presser on Monday and also responded on the question of crackdown on Jharkhand students.

âThe youth of the country have fully understood this duplicitous character of the Congress,â Pradhan said, adding that there was âno place for dictatorship in democracyâ.

His remarks came days after he stepped down as Union education minister following prolonged student protests in New Delhi and across the country over the NEET-UG paper-leak fiasco.

A day earlier, Rahul in his presser, condemned the use of force against students. He also called on the state government to engage with the protesters and resolve their concerns.

âMy message to protesting students in Jharkhand is clear. We condemn any violence against peacefully protesting students,â Rahul said.

âIt does not matter where it is happening. We condemn it, we are against it, we do not recommend it, and we do not support it. We are very clear,â Rae Bareli MP said.

Rahul maintained that peaceful protests should not be met with force and urged the Jharkhand government to continue listening to the students.

World.title: 'Speak impeccable Tamil' vs 'I have my own style': Grammar jibes set off row in Tamil Nadu assembly
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A row over Tamil Nadu finance ministerâs language and pronunciation skills during his budget speech triggered a political row in the state assembly on Monday, with the opposition members criticising his use of English and "grammatical errors".

The controversy began when MDMK MLA T M Rajendran, who won from Kadayanallur assembly constituency on the DMKâs Rising Sun symbol, pointed out "gramatical errors" in TVK minister N Marie Wilsonâs August 5 budget speech.

'Several grammatical errors'

Rajendran said Wilson had skipped several Tamil sentences and used English extensively during the speech. âAs a Tamil enthusiast, I observed in his (Marie Wilsonâs) speech that he had skipped many of the Tamil sentences.

There were several grammatical errors too,ââ Rajendran said.

âAtleast in the future, when he gets the opportunity the finance minister should speak in impeccable Tamil,â he added.

Rajendran also asked school education minister A Rajmohan to help Wilson improve his Tamil. Rajmohan, however defended the finance minister, saying there was nothing wrong with his speech. He also pointed out that leader of opposition

spoke in a plain and simple language.





'I would speak in my own style'

The remarks drew an angry response from Wilson, who defended his communication style and said his focus was on governance and the stateâs development rather than linguistic formalities.

âThe government under chief minister C Joseph Vijay has made significant achievements in the past 60-75 days, successfully bringing Rs 15,000 crores into the treasury through various reforms,â Wilson said, without elaborating.

Wilson said he had worked in the education sector for 25 to 30 years and had primarily communicated in English during his professional career.

âEarlier they were body shaming other and were insulting others based on caste and gender. Now they are insulting us over language,â Marie Wilson said.

The minister said he felt that members were targeting his communication style and background instead of focusing on his work.

He said he could not change the way he spoke simply to satisfy others.

Citing the Bible, Wilson said that while he might not be well-versed in Tamil, Christianity had taught him several languages, including the âlove language, peace language and the language of kindnessâ.

He added that he could not change his pronunciation for others and said âI would speak in my own style and that I could not change it to suit others.â

Speaker J C D Prabhakar intervened and advised Wilson to sit down and avoid getting angry.

'Tamil and English both allowed'

DMK senior leader and former minister E V Velu sought to defuse the issue, pointing out that Tamil has several dialects across the state, including differences between north and south Chennai.

Velu also stressed that Tamil Nadu followed a dual-language policy of Tamil and English.

The Speaker also noted that Rajendran himself had used the English word âbudgetâ in his speech instead of its Tamil equivalent.

Prabhakar urged members to treat the matter lightly and avoid turning language into a source of conflict in the House. He said the Assembly was a forum where multiple languages were permitted under its rules and members should focus on policy discussions rather than personal remarks.

The Speaker cited an earlier instance when then chief minister J Jayalalithaa allowed a Congress member to speak in Telugu in the Assembly.

He also pointed out that former finance minister P Thiaga Rajan had used English during earlier budget sessions.

Prabhakar said Assembly Rule 86 allows members to conduct proceedings in Tamil or English, or in both languages. He stressed that the focus should be on the intent and substance of what is being said rather than the language used.

World.title: 'Paper leaks, loss of young lives': Vijay govt passes resolution to scrap NEET in Tamil Nadu
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on Tuesday passed a resolution urging the Union government to scrap the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), with the DMK, AIADMK, Left parties and PMK supporting the move.

The lone BJP MLA staged a walkout during the proceedings.

Moving the resolution, health minister K G Arunraj said NEET was against social justice, equality and the rights of states. He said the examination had undermined medical education opportunities for students from rural and socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds.

The minister said NEET had led to the proliferation of coaching centres and the charging of exorbitant fees.

He also said the examination had shifted studentsâ focus from the school curriculum to coaching.

Arunraj said a single-day NEET examination was determining studentsâ access to higher education instead of their 12 years of school education.

Tamil Nadu finance minister Marie Wilson reiterated the demand while presenting the state Budget for 2026-27.

The state government has allocated Rs 8,393 crore to the higher education sector for 2026-27.

World.title: Watch: NDA and oppn MPs confront each other in Parliament during Jharkhand, NEET protests
World.content:
NEW DELHI: NDA and Congress-led opposition MPs staged rival protests in the Parliament complex on Tuesday and were seen face-to-face, holding placards and raising slogans against each other as security personnel formed a cordon between the two groups.

The ruling alliance accused the opposition of avoiding discussions inside the House while raising issues outside it, while the opposition demanded accountability from Union home minister Amit Shah over alleged police action against students during NEET protests.

NDA MPs marched from the Parliament Library towards Makar Dwar, raising slogans including âRahul Gandhi Jawab Doâ and âRahul Gandhi Bhago Maatâ (Rahul Gandhi, answer us, donât run away).

They accused Rahul and the opposition of avoiding a discussion in Parliament on Jharkhand student protests despite the government's decision to take up the issue.

Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi on Monday condemned the use of force against protesting students in Jharkhand.

The government had on Monday announced a discussion on student protests in different parts of the country, with Union home minister Amit Shah expected to lead the debate.





Rahul, however, questioned the government's approach, saying the country was not interested in Shah's opinion on âgeneral topicsâ and wanted to know whether he had ordered the use of pellet guns against protesting students.

The government and the opposition have also been at odds over the functioning of Parliament.

BJP leaders also questioned Rahul Gandhi's response to the alleged use of lathis and water cannons against protesting students in Jharkhand.

BJP MP Anurag Thakur said, âJustice must be done for the youth of Jharkhand. The way they were subjected to lathi-charges and atrocities reveals the mindset of Rahul Gandhi.â

On the other side, opposition MPs, including Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, MP Dimple Yadav among others staged a separate protest in the Parliament complex. They demanded accountability from HM Shah over alleged police excesses against students during the July 20 protest in Delhi.

World.title: 'Life begins at conception': Tamil Nadu Speaker sparks row over anti-abortion remarks

Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker JCD Prabhakar attended the 5th National March for Life as the chief guest on August 8 and 9.During the gathering, which protested abortion rights and advocated for the protection of unborn life, he reportedly said that âlife begins at conception," as cited by PTI.The event, hosted by the Archdiocese of Madras-Mylapore at Stella Maris College, drew more than 5,000 participants. The gathering also explicitly criticised the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act.Prabhakarâs remarks echoed global anti-abortion sentiments expressed at the event, which focused on opposing abortion rights and advocating for the protection of unborn life.The remarks prompted state Health Minister K G Arunraj to clarify on Monday that abortions can be a medical necessity and are strictly regulated under national law.Responding to reporters during a press conference to announce the MBBS/BDS rank list for 2026-27, the Health Minister sought to address the controversy, saying he was unaware of the context in which the Speaker made the remarks and urging the public not to misinterpret them."Abortion is regulated through the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act," the minister stated."Legally, as per the current law, women can legally undergo an abortion up to 20 weeks of pregnancy.In the medical field, across many circumstances, abortion is a definitive medical necessity, and it is something we must do."Asked about the constitutional and political implications of the Speakerâs anti-abortion stance, the minister sought to distinguish the stateâs health framework from Prabhakarâs personal views.âI do not know in what sense the Honourable Assembly Speaker made those comments. World.title: 'Images disturb me deeply': Congress's Sam Pitroda questions 'use of force' against Jharkhand students
World.content:
Sam Pitroda backs Jharkhand student protests

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sam Pitroda on Monday backed protesting students in Jharkhand as an agitation over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations intensified in Ranchi. Criticising the governmentâs use of lathis, tear gas and water cannons, Pitroda called for âreform, accountability and compassionâ as the protests entered their 18th day.The development comes as the Jharkhand studentsâ 'Vidhan Sabha gherao' march in Ranchi on Monday saw police use lathis and water cannons to disperse protesters. The march was organised over alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).The protesters are demanding, among other measures, the cancellation of the JSSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process.In a series of posts on X, the Indian Overseas Congress (IOC) global chairman said the grievances of young people should be addressed through dialogue."The images from Ranchi disturb me deeplyâ, he wrote.Pitroda said students should not be met with force, calling them India's future and expressing solidarity with Jharkhand's youth.In another post, Pitroda said, "Democracy requires governments to create space for peaceful dissent, dialogue and resolution."Pitroda's remarks came after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students, urging the Jharkhand government to address their grievances. The Hemant Soren-led Jharkhand government is run by a JMM-led coalition in which the Congress is a partner.Pitroda also said the protesting youth deserved to be heard respectfully and urged authorities to address their concerns over fair examinations, transparent recruitment, employment opportunities and their prospects for the future."These are not unreasonable demands. India owes its youth a system they can trustâ, he added in the postHe further said the concerns of students needed to be viewed in the context of the sacrifices made by their families."Behind every protesting student is a family that has sacrificed - often for years for education and the hope of a job.Pitroda criticised the JMM-led Jharkhand government over the handling of recruitment and examination-related grievances, saying delays in recruitment and failures in examinations risk eroding young people's trust in the system. He called for "reform, accountability and compassion" in addressing their concerns.Calling India's youth its "greatest assets", Pitroda said the country's demographic dividend could turn into frustration if education does not translate into opportunities and examinations fail to inspire confidence."We must redesign education, assessment and employment systems for this generation â not punish them for demanding change," he said.On Monday, police and protesters clashed during the march outside the Jharkhand Assembly. Police resorted to at least three rounds of lathicharge, while tear gas shells and water cannons were also used to disperse demonstrators.Injured protester alleged that police began the lathicharge without warning.The police have, however, given a different account of the events. Ranchi deputy commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri said a stone was thrown at a police jawan and alleged that some "anti-social elements" attempted to provoke police and officials during the protest.Addressing a press conference, Bhajantri said the police had exercised restraint throughout the demonstration and used "mild force" only after a situation arose in which a jawan's life was allegedly at risk.Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said most students were peaceful but alleged that a section of protesters damaged barricades and pelted stones.The protest also affected Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who was admitted to Sadar Hospital in Ranchi after taking part in the march.Mahto had been on hunger strike for nine days at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium before joining the 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march despite his deteriorating health. He was later admitted to hospital.The police action drew criticism from political leaders across party lines. On Monday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students."The use of force against students protesting in Jharkhand is wrong. Students have a right to peaceful protest, and only dialogue can yield solutions," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X, on Monday.He further urged the Jharkhand government to address the students' grievances."The Jharkhand government must continue to hear these students out and resolve their issues immediately," he added.The JPSC and JSSC examinations have been at the centre of protests by aspirants over alleged irregularities. Separately, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has registered an Enforcement Case Information Report under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act in connection with alleged irregularities in JPSC examinations.

World.title: 'New Parliament,  PM house, why not new govt schools in villages?' CJP's Dipke announces nationwide campaign
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a nationwide campaign to improve government schools in villages, seeking to address the "neglect of rural educational infrastructure".

The campaign will be launched on August 15, with the CJP calling on citizens, parents and village leaders to work together to improve basic facilities in government schools.

Dipke said he would launch the initiative from his village in Hingoli, Maharashtra, by approaching the village head and requesting him to take steps to improve government schools there.

âThe coming 15th August is our 80th Independence Day. But, if anything has been neglected or ignored the most in the last 80 years, it is the government schools in our villages,â Dipke said on Monday.

âWe have made a new Parliament, a new PM house. Why have we not been able to build new schools in our villages? Do we not consider the children of farmers and labourers the future of our country?â he asked.

Dipke said children in villages continue to face difficulties in accessing schools and basic facilities such as drinking water and toilets.

âEven today, village children have to walk a long distance to go to school. After going there, they donât find water or toilet facilities,â he said, highlighting the difficulties faced by girls in particular.





âI feel that on this 15th August, if we should pay attention to anything, if we should make a new start, we should start by improving our government schools,â he said.

The âSarpanch Challengeâ

As part of the campaign, the CJP has appealed to sarpanches across the country to take up the task of improving government schools in their respective villages.

Dipke said he would personally approach the village head in Hingoli and urged other sarpanches to do the same in their villages.

The organisation has termed the initiative the âSarpanch Challengeâ, under which it plans to publicly recognise village heads who improve their schools by sharing before-and-after photographs on its social media platforms and giving credit to the sarpanches concerned.

âWe will give you credit so that after seeing you, after seeing the schools that you have improved, many other village heads also start improving schools in their villages," Dipke said.

The CJP has also called for a citizen-led social audit of government schools.

Parents whose children study in government schools have been asked to visit the institutions and check basic facilities, including electricity, clean drinking water, functional washrooms and mid-day meals.

âYou go to your children's schools and see if basic facilities are available. See if there is electricity, waterâ¦ Do your children get washroom facilities? Do they get mid-day meals?â Dipke said.

He urged parents to record videos if basic facilities were unavailable. The CJP said it would soon issue a printable audit form through which citizens could record the facilities available at their children's schools and those that were missing.

The form will be shared through links on campaign videos on the CJP's official social media platforms and completed forms and video evidence can be emailed to the organisation.

The campaign aims to ensure that children of farmers and wage labourers studying in village schools have access to facilities comparable to those available to children in cities.

âIf not, you make videos of it. Because your children's schooling should be good. That is your fundamental right," Dipke said.

âLet us all make a promise to the children who live in villages that we will improve their schools. Together, we can do this,â he said, concluding his video with the message, âReal India lives in villagesâ.

CJP backs Jharkhand protests

In a separate video, Dipke also extended his support to Jharkhand student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who was hospitalised after his health deteriorated during a hunger strike over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.

Calling the alleged police action against protesters âcruel and inhumanâ, Dipke drew a parallel with student protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. âBe it Jantar Mantar or Jharkhand, such police brutality against students is cruel and inhuman,â he said.

âCJP stands firmly with Devendra bhai and his struggle. He is a true hero. We salute his courage and strength!â he added.

Mahto has been at the centre of the ongoing JPSC-JSSC agitation in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. He had been on an indefinite hunger strike and joined the students' Vidhan Sabha gherao march on Monday, arriving at the protest in an ambulance as his health deteriorated.

World.title: Man hacks girlfriend, her mother to death near Palladam
World.content:
A 42-year-old woman and her 22-year-old daughter were hacked to death allegedly by the latter’s boyfriend following a dispute over their relationship near Palladam in Tiruppur district on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) morning.

The deceased were identified as Dhanalakshmi, 42, of Pachapalayam near Palladam, and her daughter Poovarasi, 22. Poovarasi was working at a mechanic showroom in the locality.

According to the police, Poovarasi had been in a relationship with Akshay, 27, a college student from Pattiveerampatti in Dindigul district, who was studying in Coimbatore. The two had reportedly been in a relationship for around four years after meeting on social media.

Poovarasi’s family was opposed to their relationship. Police said Akshay went to Poovarasi’s house on Tuesday morning and picked an argument with Poovarasi and her mother Dhanalakshmi. During the altercation, he allegedly attacked both women with a sickle, killing them.

Palladam police reached the spot after being alerted and conducted an inquiry. The bodies were sent to a government hospital for postmortem.

A case was registered and Akshay was arrested and remanded in judicial custody. Further investigation is under way.

World.title: Messi visit row: Kerala’s UDF govt weighs anti-corruption probe into Argentina football match plan under previous LDF regime
World.content:
The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Kerala on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) appeared poised to order an anti-corruption investigation into the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government’s “bungled attempt” to bring the 2021 FIFA World Cup-winning Argentina team and its iconic captain, Lionel Messi, for a ‘friendly exhibition’ match at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Kochi in 2025.

State Sports and Youth Affairs Minister O.J. Janeesh told reporters in New Delhi that he had submitted the supposedly “damning” inquiry report (vetted by Sports Department Special Secretary N. Prasanth) to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan for further action. Mr Janeesh said the internal report detailed “a series of grave violations.”

According to government officials, the report raised several regulatory red flags that warrant exhaustive Central and State investigations, possibly conducted in parallel.

Charges

The charges, they said, reportedly included massive service tax fraud on foreign remittances, contraventions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), abuse of power resulting in loss to the public exchequer, and “shady financial transactions” involving offshore entities, among other charges that could potentially trigger the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) and GST department probes.

According to government officials, Mr Prasanth’s inquiry centred on former Kerala Sports Minister V. Abdurahiman’s big-ticket announcement in 2023 that the Kerala government had partnered with a private sponsor, a television news broadcasting company, to host the Argentine football team led by Messi at “no cost to the public exchequer” in 2025 ahead of the 2026 Assembly elections.

Mr Abdurahiman also led a high-profile delegation to Spain, reportedly costing the public exchequer an estimated ₹14 crore, to meet Argentine Football Association (AFA) office-bearers, ratcheting up expectations among football lovers in the State.

The private sponsor further heightened feverish public anticipation by claiming that he had transferred ₹126 crore to the AFA’s account in advance of the visit.

However, neither Messi nor the Argentine team showed up in Kerala in 2025, pivoting the public enthusiasm for the World Cup-winning squad and Messi into outrage and anger against the LDF government.

The ensuing public fury caused Mr Abdurahiman, the event’s sponsor and the then-ruling dispensation to seek political cover by alleging that AFA had broken faith with the State’s football lovers by “unilaterally and inexplicably” withdrawing from the ₹250-crore contractual agreement struck by the parties, including the LDF government, in Spain.

Messi’s “no show” in Kochi also ignited a fierce political backlash, with the UDF, then in the Opposition, accusing the then LDF government of hoodwinking football lovers.

Congress and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) social media handles launched a viral “Missing Messi” campaign, mocking the previous LDF government’s “fumbled attempt to slyly use the iconic footballer as the LDF’s political surrogate at the hustings to win over the young demographic in the run-up to the 2026 Assembly polls.”

According to government officials, the report doubted the private sponsor’s claim that the entity had channelled ₹126 crores to AFA through a US-based intermediary “under investigation”, citing a lack of documentary and banking evidence.

They said the report also flagged the absence of a legally binding contract or legitimate tripartite agreement between AFA, the Kerala government, and the private sponsor.

World.title: Ebola deaths cross 2,000 in Democratic Republic of Congo
World.content:
Democratic Republic of Congo said on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) that confirmed Ebola deaths had reached 2,011, the latest grim milestone in what health ‌officials have described as the fastest-spreading outbreak on record.

The latest data from Congo’s public health institute, ‌seen by Reuters, also reported 4,381 confirmed cases across ‌five provinces. Delayed ⁠detection, conflict and strained health services have helped ⁠the virus spread more rapidly than in previous outbreaks.

The current outbreak, Congo’s 17th, is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for ​which there are no ‌approved vaccines or treatments.

The World Health Organization has declared the outbreak, which has also led to cases in neighbouring Uganda, a public health emergency of international concern.

A study ‌published last month in the journal Science found ​that transmission may have begun in January or earlier in Ituri province, identifying more than 500 ⁠suspected cases between mid-January and May 15.

Shortages of medical supplies and insecurity in affected areas have complicated efforts to trace ‌contacts, isolate patients and curb transmission.

The Congolese government data shows that only West Africa’s 2014 to 2016 Ebola outbreak was bigger, with 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths recorded across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone, according to the World Health Organization. It took nearly five months from the declaration ‌of that outbreak to hit 1,000 deaths, whereas Congo’s current outbreak ​has hit 2,000 deaths in less than three months.

In an Ebola outbreak in Congo from 2018 to ⁠2020, it took a little over 12 months to hit ⁠2,000 deaths. In the current outbreak, deaths have jumped from 1,000 to 2,000 in less than ‌a month, further underscoring how quickly the virus is spreading.
