World.title: Armenian Catholicos Garegin II attends first hearing in criminal trial
World.content:
Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

A court in Armenia‘s Armavir region has begun hearing the criminal case against the Catholicos of All Armenians and six bishops who serve on the Supreme Spiritual Council. Garegin II attended the hearing in person.

Clergy members and politicians gathered outside the courthouse. Lawmakers from the opposition Armenia Alliance and I Have Honour Alliance left parliament during the afternoon and travelled to Etchmiadzin to show their support for the Catholicos. Dozens of worshippers also gathered outside, periodically chanting “Your Holiness” and singing traditional Armenian church hymns (sharakans).

Prosecutors accuse the Catholicos and the senior clergy of obstructing the enforcement of a court ruling.

Garegin II removed Bishop Gevorg Saroyan, head of the Masyatsotn Diocese, from his post. Saroyan is one of the senior clerics who joined Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s campaign to “reform the Church”. The bishop challenged his dismissal in court. The court ordered his temporary reinstatement as head of the diocese until it reaches a final decision in the case. However, before the court could rule on the merits, the Supreme Spiritual Council, led by the Catholicos, also defrocked him. The council argued that the courts have no jurisdiction over the Church’s internal affairs.

Lawyer Ara Zohrabyan says the Catholicos faces criminal prosecution for carrying out his “ecclesiastical and canonical duties”.

He argues that state interference in the Catholicos’s decisions violates the principle of Church autonomy, the constitutional relationship between the state and the Church, and freedom of religion.

“In this criminal case, the court will examine not only the charges against specific individuals, but also another fundamental question: whether the secular authorities can interfere in the internal life of the Church and criminalise the exercise of the canonical authority of the Catholicos of All Armenians,” the lawyer said.

The trial comes after tensions between the government and the Church steadily escalated.

About a year ago, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called for the Catholicos to step down. He first argued that Garegin II could not lead the Church because he had broken his vow of celibacy and had a daughter. He later accused the Catholicos of having links to foreign intelligence services. The ruling Civil Contract party has also included the removal of the “de facto head of the Church” in its election manifesto.

Members of the ruling party accuse the Church of interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy. The parliamentary opposition rejects that claim. Opposition lawmakers argue that it is the government that is unlawfully interfering in the Church’s affairs.

First hearing ends after 30 minutes as judge recuses himself

Shortly after the hearing began, Judge Hakob Manukyan announced that part of the proceedings would take place behind closed doors because they would involve “personal information”. He said the information concerned both himself and the Catholicos’s lawyer.

“A few minutes later, lawyer Ara Zohrabyan told journalists: “The judge has recused himself. He has withdrawn from hearing this case.”

According to Zohrabyan, the judge said he had once granted him his licence to practise law, which could “raise doubts about his impartiality”. Zohrabyan said he did not believe this constituted valid grounds for recusal.

“However, he refused to take part in this disgraceful trial. The very fact that the Catholicos is standing trial is deeply troubling. The case will now go to another judge.”

After the hearing, the Catholicos of All Armenians and his supporters headed to the cathedral to attend a church service and pray together.

Garegin II: “The authorities are trying to bring the Church under their control”

After the service, the Catholicos addressed those gathered outside the cathedral. He said the authorities were taking steps to undermine the Church’s authority, restrict its autonomy and bring it under their control.

“The authorities are persecuting the Church and the clergy. They have arrested and restricted the freedom of a number of clergymen, benefactors and other patriotic individuals through unlawful and fabricated criminal cases,” he said.

The Catholicos dismissed the charges against himself and the six clergymen as groundless.

“We remain steadfast in our faith and determination to defend our rights, which are guaranteed both by our country’s Constitution and by the fundamental principles of international law.”

Opposition declares a “day of shame”

Marianna Gakhramanyan, an MP from the opposition I Have Honour Alliance, said:

“Today is a day of shame. The Catholicos of All Armenians, our spiritual father and the head of our Church, is standing trial in Etchmiadzin. It is shameful and unprecedented. This is an attack not only on the independence of the Armenian Apostolic Church but also on Armenia’s Constitution, which clearly states that the political authorities have no right to interfere in the affairs of the Church and that the Church is separate from the state.”

“Who is defending the Church – us or you?” asks ruling party MP

Commenting on opposition lawmakers who came to support the Catholicos, Civil Contract MP Artur Hovhannisyan said:

“The Church has begun interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy.”

He also referred to the allegations that the Catholicos had violated his vow of celibacy:

“We are the ones standing with the Church. We are the ones defending the Church. You are defending clergymen who broke their vow of celibacy, who engage in politics and use religion and the Church to protect themselves from the consequences of breaking that vow and taking part in politics. Anyone who has broken the vow of celibacy should leave the Church.”

The ruling Civil Contract party’s election manifesto also outlines plans to reform the Church. Under the proposal, the “de facto head of the Church”, as Pashinyan’s team refers to the Catholicos, should leave office. The plan calls for the election of a locum tenens, the adoption of a new Church charter containing “mechanisms to preserve centuries-old traditions”, and, ultimately, the election of a new Catholicos.

Comment

Political analyst Tigran Grigoryan told Reuters:

“Pashinyan has come to see the Church as a political threat and as an institution capable of supporting the opposition and various political parties in their efforts to gain power.

“The case against the clergy fits into a broader pattern of selective justice pursued by Pashinyan’s government, under which leading opposition figures have been arrested and some of their property has been confiscated by the state.”

Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

World.title: Azerbaijan FM in Kyiv: gas for Ukraine, visit to Irpin, Ukrainian drones
World.content:
Azerbaijani FM visits Ukraine

Azerbaijan‘s Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov paid an official visit to Ukraine on 6 August.

It was the first visit by an Azerbaijani foreign minister to Kyiv since the start of Russia‘s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Bayramov began his visit with a trip to Irpin, where he viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones and laid a wreath at a memorial to fallen defenders at Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry.

He also held meetings with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, President Volodymyr Zelensky, Head of the Presidential Office Andriy Yermak, Defence Intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and National Security and Defence Council Secretary Ihor Klymenko.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

One of the most notable announcements was Azerbaijan’s stated willingness to supply Ukraine with natural gas if needed.

The two sides also discussed the possible use of Ukraine’s underground gas storage facilities to strengthen regional energy security.

These developments are significant both regionally and internationally, particularly in the context of Azerbaijan’s relations with Russia.

In mid-July, Bayramov met Sergei Lavrov in Moscow and said the “difficult period” in bilateral relations was over and that ties had been fully normalised. A few weeks later, in Kyiv, he reaffirmed Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also signalling Baku’s interest in expanding energy cooperation.

The visit illustrates Baku’s multi-vector foreign policy. While maintaining dialogue with Russia, Azerbaijan has continued to provide humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and has expressed its readiness to support the country in the energy sector if required.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

Symbolic and practical significance of the Irpin visit

Irpin was one of the towns where the Russian advance on Kyiv was halted in 2022. Hundreds of civilians were killed during the fighting, and more than 70% of the town’s housing stock was destroyed.

Azerbaijan has contributed to Irpin’s reconstruction.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

The minister laid flowers at the bust of academician Zarifa Aliyeva in the park named after her, and visited the Zarifa Aliyeva Linguistic Lyceum and Irpin Central City Polyclinic, both rebuilt with Azerbaijan’s support. He was also briefed on future reconstruction projects, including plans to restore the town’s House of Culture.

In his statement, Zelensky said Bayramov had visited a school, a hospital and a rehabilitation centre supported by Azerbaijan. The visit to Irpin was seen as a demonstration of humanitarian solidarity with Ukraine, as well as Azerbaijan’s willingness to share its experience in rebuilding territories recovered from occupation.

I received Azerbaijan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, @Bayramov_Jeyhun. This is the Minister’s first visit to Ukraine since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion. He began his visit in Irpin, where he visited a school, a hospital, and a rehabilitation center supported by… pic.twitter.com/7HTLIaz3EF — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) August 6, 2026

The visit to a town devastated by Russian forces, together with Bayramov’s review of reconstruction efforts and Azerbaijan’s continued support, was seen as underscoring Baku’s intention to reaffirm its longstanding position despite the “normalisation” of relations with Moscow, particularly its commitment to the principle of territorial integrity.

Following the official welcoming ceremony at the Foreign Ministry, Bayramov and Sybiha viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones. They then laid a wreath at the Memorial to the Fallen Defenders of Ukraine and observed a moment of silence in their honour.

Meetings and gas supply pledge

During expanded talks with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, the two sides discussed their strategic partnership, trade, energy, transport, humanitarian cooperation and regional security. Bayramov reiterated the need for an early end to the fighting and a diplomatic settlement based on international law, while reaffirming Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders.

He said Azerbaijan’s total humanitarian assistance to Ukraine had exceeded 50 million US dollars. Bayramov also highlighted reconstruction projects in Irpin and rehabilitation programmes for children.

During his meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky, the discussions focused on Russian attacks, the situation in the Black Sea, the disruption of grain export routes, defence cooperation, and cooperation in the energy, oil and gas, and agricultural sectors.

Zelensky thanked Azerbaijan for its energy and humanitarian assistance, as well as for maintaining constructive dialogue. Bayramov, in turn, spoke about the post-conflict situation in the South Caucasus and reconstruction efforts in the territories regained by Azerbaijan.

As part of his official visit to Ukraine 🇺🇦, FM of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 @Bayramov_Jeyhun visited the Embassy of Azerbaijan in Kyiv.



The Minister met with the Embassy staff and received a comprehensive briefing on the Mission’s activities. pic.twitter.com/UPqN5Hn9rx — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

At a joint press conference, particular attention was drawn to Bayramov’s remarks on possible gas supplies: “If the need arises, we will be ready to supply gas to our friendly Ukraine.”

He highlighted SOCAR’s long-standing presence on the Ukrainian market, as well as the importance of Ukraine’s underground gas storage system – the largest in Europe – for regional energy security.

The statement can be seen as signalling Azerbaijan’s willingness to contribute to the diversification of Ukraine’s energy supplies, while also supporting alternative routes for Caspian gas exports to Europe. Against the backdrop of Russia’s strikes on energy infrastructure in southern Ukraine, Baku’s offer also underscores the importance of competition and diversification in the energy sector.

During meetings with Kyrylo Budanov and Ihor Klymenko, the sides also discussed regional and international security, as well as prospects for energy cooperation. They reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of state sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inviolability of internationally recognised borders.

Expert: “Azerbaijan will continue to provide Ukraine with political, economic and humanitarian support”

lkhan Shahinoglu, head of the Atlas Research Centre and a political commentator considered close to the Azerbaijani authorities, wrote that the visit is being closely watched by Russia:

The Kremlin will closely monitor Jeyhun Bayramov’s meetings in Kyiv. Azerbaijan’s partnership with any country is an exclusive sovereign right, and no other state has the right to interfere in that process.

At the same time, Russia, which is waging a war of conquest against Ukraine, closely watches those who cooperate with Kyiv. President Ilham Aliyev‘s response to the same question from Ukrainian journalist Gordon, asked at the Shusha Global Media Forum two years in a row – that ‘Ukraine should not reconcile itself to occupation’ – angered chauvinistic circles in Russia. They believe Azerbaijan should accept the annexation of Crimea and the occupation of Ukrainian territories.

Just as Jeyhun Bayramov visited Moscow some time ago, he has now travelled to Kyiv. Ukraine is Azerbaijan’s partner, and Baku will continue to provide it with political, economic and humanitarian support.”

World.title: Giga Avaliani case: Two more arrested 10 months after Georgian teacher’s murder
World.content:
Two more arrested in Giga Avaliani murder case

Two more suspects have been identified in the high-profile murder case of a 28-year-old teacher in Georgia. On 5 August 2026, two teenage girls – Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili – were arrested.

Giga Avaliani, a mathematics teacher, was killed in October 2025. Five people have already been convicted over his murder, while the trial of a sixth defendant is still under way. With the arrest of the two girls, the total number of suspects in the case has risen to eight – all of them minors.

The arrests of Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili, after several convictions had already been secured, mark an unexpected and significant development in the Giga Avaliani case.

Nia Imnadze was one of Giga Avaliani’s former students and the girlfriend of the principal defendant, Aleksandre Gabashvili. Prosecutors accuse her of incitement to commit the crime.

According to local media, Anastasia Beruashvili is a friend of both Nia Imnadze and another convicted defendant, Giorgi Rikadze. She has been charged with failing to report the crime.

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics tutor, was returning home late on 1 October 2025 when he was attacked outside his apartment building. He fell into a coma following the assault and died on 24 October without regaining consciousness. Investigators say the attack was motivated by jealousy and what they describe as “unwanted communication with a girl”. The defendants have given a similar account. According to their version of events, Avaliani sent sexually explicit messages to his student Nia Imnadze, who told her boyfriend, prompting him to confront the teacher. Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, rejects that account. She says Nia had been skipping lessons and that Avaliani informed the girl’s mother, angering the student. According to Kupatadze, the attack was planned afterwards.

The Giga Avaliani case has become one of Georgia’s most high-profile criminal cases in recent years. Much of the public attention surrounding it has been driven by Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, who campaigned for what she said should be a thorough and impartial investigation. Her efforts also helped generate significant public pressure over the handling of the case.

From the outset, Kupatadze maintained that Nia Imnadze bore primary responsibility for what had happened and repeatedly called for her arrest. The recent detention of the two girls has therefore raised new questions.

But the key question remains: if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, why were the two girls not arrested earlier? Was their detention the result of new evidence, or did it come only after sustained public pressure and Eka Kupatadze’s campaign?

Detention of two girls

Both girls were arrested late on the night of 5 August, in what appeared to be coordinated operations. News of the arrests first emerged through a video of Nia Imnadze’s detention, which was released by her lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili.

The footage is deeply distressing. It shows a large number of police officers arriving at Nia’s home. Her mother, visibly distressed, pounds on the front door, shouting: “Come in, all of you!”, “Maniacs!”, “Murderers!”, “Do you know that Niako is innocent?!”

The girl’s father, meanwhile, tells the police: “You are going to make me do something the whole of Georgia will be talking about. If you treat my child so unjustly, I will do it.”

Police officers try to calm the distraught parents.

“Why are you taking my child? On what grounds? What does the court order say?!” the mother asks.

“The lawyer has reviewed the court order,” one of the officers replies.

“Giorgi, on what grounds are they arresting her?” the mother asks the lawyer.

“On the basis of a court order containing only formal wording, nothing specific,” the lawyer replies.

Nia sits in the hallway on a sofa, curled up with her face buried in her hands. The video is being filmed by her lawyer, who occasionally strokes her hair.

Shortly after the video was released, reports began circulating on social media that the second girl, Anastasia Beruashvili, had also been detained. No footage of her arrest was made public, but the Ministry of Internal Affairs later confirmed that she had been taken into custody.

During her arrest, Nia Imnadze became unwell and was taken to hospital, where she spent the night. On 6 August, she was transferred to a pre-trial detention centre. Anastasia Beruashvili was also taken there.

Minors charged in Giga Avaliani's murder case in Georgia – read more Five people have already been convicted in connection with Giga Avaliani’s murder: Aleksandre Gabashvili – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. He was the principal defendant in the case and was found guilty of organising a group assault and intentionally inflicting grievous bodily harm as part of a group, resulting in the victim’s death. Giorgi Rikadze – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. A friend of Aleksandre Gabashvili, he was convicted on the same charges. Demetere Chikovani – sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was convicted of attempted intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm in the Avaliani case, as well as organising group violence in connection with the case and four other incidents. Ani Naskidashvili – sentenced to five years and three months’ imprisonment. She was found guilty of failing to report a particularly serious crime. Another minor – sentenced to three years’ imprisonment. He was convicted of giving false testimony. The nature of the false statements has not been disclosed. His case was heard behind closed doors, lawyers involved in the proceedings are bound by a non-disclosure order, and the teenager’s parents have declined to speak to the media. According to TV Pirveli, the boy is named Luka Klatkin. Giorgi Malania – arrested in July 2026 and charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. Malania is the son of a former senior Interior Ministry official, who served as deputy interior minister between 2016 and 2019. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered.

Eka Kupatadze’s reaction

“Georgia has won another battle against the killers of a healthy, innocent and talented young man – Giga Avaliani!” Eka Kupatadze said in response to the girls’ arrests.

Giga Avaliani’s family has always maintained that those who carried out the attack were not the only people involved. They have consistently called on investigators to identify and prosecute all those who may have played a role in the crime.

The family has paid particular attention to the alleged role of the two girls. Eka Kupatadze has repeatedly said that they knew the attack was being planned.

Until recently, however, prosecutors had taken no apparent action against additional suspects, prompting repeated criticism of the investigation from Avaliani’s family.

Kupatadze even appealed for help to Ekaterine Khvedelidze, the wife of Bidzina Ivanishvili, the founder of the ruling party and widely regarded as Georgia’s “informal ruler”. Khvedelidze replied to her letter, expressing sympathy and support for the mother who had lost her son.

“As far as I am aware, the investigation has not yet been completed. I am confident that the relevant state authorities will see it through to the end and that all the circumstances will be thoroughly examined, so that no question surrounding the terrible tragedy that has befallen you remains unanswered,” Ekaterine Khvedelidze wrote in her reply.

Formal charges

On the evening of 6 August, both girls were formally charged.

Nia Imnadze at the time of her arrest

Nia Imnadze has been charged with incitement to intentionally inflict grievous bodily harm committed by a group. The offence carries a maximum sentence of 13 years’ imprisonment.

Anastasia Beruashvili has been charged with failing to report a particularly serious crime, an offence punishable by up to seven years’ imprisonment.

Under Georgian law, sentences imposed on minors are reduced by one quarter.

“The investigation conducted by the Ministry of Internal Affairs under the supervision of the Prosecutor’s Office established that, in September 2025, Nia Imnadze began taking mathematics lessons with Giga Avaliani. The accused, Nia Imnadze, told her friends Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Malania that her teacher, Giga Avaliani, had allegedly shown her excessive attention. By doing so, the accused incited Aleksandre Gabashvili to attack Giga Avaliani together with his accomplices,” the Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement.

According to the statement, Aleksandre Gabashvili, together with Giorgi Rikadze, Giorgi Malania and Demetere Chikovani, “decided to act on that incitement.”

What defence says

The defence has denied all the charges.

According to Nia Imnadze’s lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili, there is no evidence in the case to support the allegation that she incited the attack.

The lawyer also rejected reports that prosecutors had obtained data and messages from Meta, and that the arrests followed an examination of those materials.

“Criminal proceedings cannot be based on suspicion. They must be based on lawfully obtained evidence, and no other standard can override that principle,” Lekishvili told reporters.

Ketevan Vardanashvili, the lawyer representing Anastasia Beruashvili, made similar arguments. She said Anastasia had not witnessed any crime and that she and Nia Imnadze had seen each other only once, for a few minutes.

“They had no friendship and no contact,” the lawyer said.

As for Anastasia’s relationship with the convicted defendant Giorgi Rikadze, Vardanashvili said that “even if she was his girlfriend, that does not mean she had any knowledge of the crime.”

Complaint or incitement?

The arrests of the two girls have sparked intense debate on social media. Many commentators agree that everyone responsible for Giga Avaliani’s death should be held accountable and that justice should be served. Many have also expressed sympathy for Eka Kupatadze.

At the same time, some have questioned the actions of the law enforcement authorities. They have asked whether prosecutors have sufficiently strong evidence against the two girls, particularly Nia Imnadze, who faces a lengthy prison sentence if convicted.

The Prosecutor’s Office statement says only that Nia Imnadze told her friends that Giga Avaliani had allegedly shown her excessive attention. It does not explain whether she knew an attack was being planned or whether she urged her boyfriend to take any specific action.

“Does complaining to friends amount to incitement?” some social media users have asked.

Others have also questioned why, if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, the girls were arrested only 10 months after the murder. Some have asked whether the arrests were prompted by Eka Kupatadze’s campaign, and whether political influence may have played a role.

Those questions also remain unanswered.

Timeline of Giga Avaliani's case – read more 1 October 2025 – The attack

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics teacher, was attacked outside his home in Tbilisi. 24 October 2025 – Death

After spending 23 days in a coma, Giga Avaliani died. November–December 2025 – First arrests

Four minors were arrested: Aleksandre Gabashvili, Giorgi Rikadze, Demetere Chikovani and Ani Naskidashvili. April 2026 – First convictions

Tbilisi City Court found Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Rikadze guilty and sentenced each to 10 years and six months’ imprisonment. Demetere Chikovani was sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was later convicted over separate violent offences committed at a different time, increasing his total sentence to nine years and nine months. June 2026 – Another conviction

The court sentenced Ani Naskidashvili to five years and three months’ imprisonment for failing to report the crime. July 2026 – Another arrest

Giorgi Malania was arrested. According to prosecutors, he was charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered. August 2026 – Two more arrests

Two more minor girls were arrested: Nia Imnadze, Giga Avaliani’s former student and the girlfriend of the principal convicted defendant, and Anastasia Beruashvili, described as a friend of Nia Imnadze and the girlfriend of the second convicted defendant.

Broader picture

From the outset, the Giga Avaliani case came to represent more than a single criminal investigation.

It exposed a range of systemic problems, most notably a lack of public trust in investigative authorities. The case also highlighted shortcomings in Georgia’s juvenile justice system, as well as concerns over the protection of the rights of both victims and defendants.

Many observers questioned the release of footage showing Nia Imnadze’s arrest, particularly as it was made public by her lawyer. Some argued that the video was intended to generate public sympathy for his client.

“Unfortunately, public trust in the justice system – the police, the Prosecutor’s Office, the courts and other institutions – is now so low that victims, defendants and lawyers increasingly see shaping public opinion as the only way to obtain justice. They then seek to use public pressure to their advantage,” lawyer Londa Toloraia wrote.

In her view, this reflects a profound crisis affecting both citizens and the justice system itself.

“You no longer trust the state, even when it may actually be making a lawful decision.”

Toloraia also raised a number of questions about the arrests of the two girls: What evidence were they based on? Why did they take place 10 months after the murder? And why were they carried out at night, when Georgian law restricts procedural actions during nighttime hours, particularly in cases involving minors?

“How much influence does public opinion have over the justice system? A great deal. It is extremely difficult to withstand public pressure. And where institutions are fully politicised, it becomes virtually impossible to make a decision that is unpopular with the public,” she argued.

She stressed that legal standards must be upheld even when dealing with those accused of serious crimes – especially when the defendants are minors.

The Avaliani case has also exposed a darker side of public reaction. Following Nia Imnadze’s arrest, social media was flooded with hostile comments directed at both her and her family. Many users described her as the main culprit and called for severe punishment. Others went further, posting comments about the suffering they believed awaited her in prison.

A second group of social media users expressed concern about the tone of those comments. Toloraia addressed the debate in a lengthy social media post.

“Children are not born criminals. Before demanding that they be lynched, we should first ask why they became who they are,” she wrote, adding that juvenile crime in Georgia has reached one of its highest levels in recent years. She argued that the state’s response has focused on opening a “special prison” for children rather than preventing youth crime. A state in which parents who have lost a child must seek justice through public mobilisation, while institutions make decisions according to fluctuations in public pressure, is a broken state,” Toloraia concluded.

World.title: Cats confirm Kolodjashnij unavailable to play amid concussion waiver saga
World.content:
The player at the centre of a concussion waiver controversy, Geelong's Jake Kolodjashnij, will not play this weekend as the club prepares to find out whether it will face sanctions.

It emerged last Thursday that the Cats struck a secret agreement with a player, who had had a history of concussions.

Kolodjashnij went public confirming he was the player involved.

The waiver has since been removed from his contract.

"Geelong Cats defender Jake Kolodjashnij will be unavailable for selection at AFL or VFL level this weekend," the club said a statement late on Tuesday.

"The care and wellbeing of Jake remains the club's priority, and the club will continue to support him and his family through this period."

The Cats had until the end of Tuesday to respond to the "please explain" from the AFL over the concussion waiver that Kolodjashnij signed but which was never seen by the AFL or the AFLPA.

Geelong Cats board holds crisis meeting over concussion deal Geelong is about to reply to the AFL's please explain as the Cats brace for a potential massive penalty over the secret concussion deal with Jake Kolodjashnij.

Amid speculation over the futures of Geelong chief executive Steve Hocking and AFL chairman Craig Drummond, the club board had held a crisis meeting on Monday to work out its response to the league.

Hocking was Cats chief executive and Drummond was the club president when the deal was struck two years ago with Koladjashnij.

The Geelong defender signed a waiver that meant he effectively took on legal responsibility for future brain trauma in a bid to indemnify the club and its medical staff from potential court action.

ABC Sport Daily podcast ABC Sport Daily is your daily sports conversation. We dive into the biggest story of the day and get you up to speed with everything else that's making headlines.

Media reports on Tuesday said that the AFL Commission had hired independent legal counsel to help determine whether the Cats should face sanctions over the issue.

The 31-year-old Kolodjashnij was drafted by the club in 2013 and he has played 209 games for Geelong.

He last played at AFL level for the Cats against GWS a month ago.

His twin brother Kade, who played for Gold Coast and Melbourne, was forced to retire in 2020 due to concussion issues.

World.title: Sydney fugitive arrested in Lebanon accused of running crime syndicate
World.content:
For years, fugitive George Dib had been a mystery.

The son of a respected service station entrepreneur, Mr Dib first appeared on the radar of law enforcement in 2013, then he vanished.

But Australian authorities had been watching.

Mr Dib, arrested last week in Lebanon, is now facing the possibility of spending decades in a Middle Eastern jail over claims he directed a global organised crime syndicate while on the run.

"He is suspected of brokering and organising multiple drug shipments to Australia on behalf of a wide range of criminal syndicates from around the world during the past 11 years," the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said after his capture in Lebanon last week.

His father is not accused of any wrongdoing.

Fugitives join forces overseas

For more than a decade, George Dib has been the source of underworld and police intrigue.

Though never convicted of a crime, Mr Dib was suspected to be part of the "Aussie Cartel", before it was systematically dismantled in Türkiye in 2023.

But according to an intelligence file from the NSW Crime Commission obtained by the ABC, Mr Dib is accused of being a main player in another offshore drug conglomerate.

A NSW Police mugshot of Rafat Alameddine, who has since fled to Lebanon. (Supplied: NSW Police)

The report names Mr Dib alongside fellow Lebanese fugitives Bilal Haouchar and Alameddine crime family boss Rafat Alameddine among other alleged Sydney criminals who joined forces.

Alameddine is wanted by NSW Police accused of two murders at the height of the Alameddines' gang war with the Hamzy family in 2021.

Haouchar himself was sentenced to eight years in jail by a Beirut court in May 2025 for a raft of drug crimes he committed while on the run from Australia.

Haouchar remains locked up in a Lebanese jail after AFP intelligence helped to jail him there. (Supplied: NSW Police)

Mr Dib, Alameddine and Haouchar are accused of sending threatening messages dubbed 'AUS weekly market updates' to Sydney's criminal milieu "in an attempt to set the distribution price of cocaine at $225,000 per kilogram".

Fall of 'The Commission'

It is alleged Mr Dib's coalition of criminals' rise came as another toppled.

The "AUS weekly market updates" landed in the inboxes of gangsters across Sydney in June 2023.

Just days earlier, the final domino of rival drug cartel "The Commission" fell when Alen Moradian was shot dead inside a Bondi car park.

Crime boss Alen Moradian. (Supplied: Nine Entertainment)

The Commission operated under a similar rule of law, spreading similar threatening message throughout the underworld through 2022 to 2023.

"To the drop kick wannabe gangsters who just called out the Commission. "You shouldn't try to claim things you did not know. "We have been dominating Sydney for the past 3 years now and like puppy dogs you have all submitted each time. "We are well aware who is responsible, writing up that message to throw the scene off won't work. "And you/they/them pop your head out of hiding you can bet your dollar we will be there to chop it off. "The weak dog who wrote that message has most likely paid us before and now feeling tough, nevertheless no stone will unturned. No friend will be loyal. "Watch this and you will know what we are about."

Though its authors were not clarified in the NSW Crime Commission intelligence, the following message was spread the day after Moradian was killed.

"To every one trying to call the shots that are hiding in different countries and playing with NSW prices. "We regret to inform your commission we control the prices in NSW from now on. "This is not just a warning but a threat to everyone who thinks they can run the streets here. "All NSW crews have come together to end your so called commission. Please remember the bullets dont rust here especially when you guys want to threaten familys we will also not toelerate this and will respond with kidnapping knee capping and if we hear any of your crews are trying to control prices under your guidelines we will come after anyone from your commission. "You guys will now follow our rules and respect us prices will be dropping at anyones will … "Thank you."

Mr Dib, nicknamed "Junior", according to Lebanese media, was picked up by the Information Branch of the Internal Security Force last week during a night-time raid.

With him in custody are about a dozen figures with links to Sydney's organised crime scene, sources told the ABC.

The intelligence that helped capture Mr Dib was provided by the AFP to Lebanese authorities by Operation Gain.

The unit is credited with taking down the "Aussie Cartel", led by drug lord Hakan Ayik out of Istanbul in 2023, and disrupting the activities of several wanted fugitives.

World.title: Alleged 2007 murder at Adelaide party involved 'payback', court told
World.content:
A man standing trial for murder over a fatal birthday party stabbing almost 20 years ago was allegedly among a group of men who stormed the celebrations seeking "payback", a court has heard.

Kimlong Rim, 38, is standing trial in South Australia's Supreme Court after pleading not guilty to the murder of Thea Kheav, 21, outside a party at Parafield Gardens, in Adelaide's north, in December 2007.

Opening the trial on Tuesday, prosecutor Kos Lesses told the jury that while Mr Rim did not inflict the fatal stab wound, he was among a group of four men accused of murdering Mr Kheav.

He said Mr Kheav was a guest at the 18th birthday party, which he had attended with his brothers.

"An argument broke out with one of the Kheav brothers and one of the men from the accused's group," Mr Lesses said.

He told the jury that that man had left the party "in an angry state" but later returned in a convoy of cars with "a large group of men", including Mr Rim and three others allegedly involved in the murder.

"[They] armed themselves with bottles and planks of wood, along with a machete-type knife," Mr Lesses said.

"They arrived at that party as a group and it's alleged they disrupted the party as a group. It's alleged they were working as a team, or a group.

"As a result of that group attack, Thea Kheav was fatally stabbed and died at the scene of this birthday party."

Kimlong Rim (left) is standing trial after pleading not guilty to the 2007 murder of Thea Kheav. (ABC News)

Mr Lesses told the jury the altercation took part in two stages, beginning when Mr Kheav was first struck with a bottle while standing next to a woman.

The jury was also told the second stage involved Mr Kheav's attempt to flee into the backyard of the house.

Mr Lesses said Mr Kheav had tried to climb over gates, but he was pulled to the ground where he was "kicked and punched, along with being stabbed in the chest with a long-bladed knife".

Crime about 'payback', court told

Mr Lesses said that despite the efforts of paramedics, Mr Kheav was unable to be resuscitated.

His cause of death was later determined to be a single stab wound to his chest, but he also had other injuries on his body, including a cut to his face.

Mr Lesses said the alleged crime was "borne out of a retaliation".

"It's about an armed group of men who retaliated by attending as a group to disrupt the party and effect payback on one of the Kheav brothers," Mr Lesses said.

Police attended the scene after a party was held at a Parafield Gardens house. (ABC News: ABC News)

Mr Lesses told the jury the alleged murder weapon was never recovered but had been described as "looking like a machete".

Mr Rim's defence barrister, Ryan Williams SC, told the jury it was not disputed his client was at the party and had "engaged in deplorable behaviour", but he said Mr Rim was not a murderer.

"What is in dispute is this idea that he is a murderer," he said.

" Put simply, ladies and gentlemen, the issues in dispute do not concern whether or not he, together with others, acted generally angrily, violently or whatever … but whether what he did, what he actually had in his mind, make him a murderer. "

Justice Rachael Gray, who is presiding over the trial, urged the 14-person jury to keep an open mind until it retires to consider a verdict.

The trial is expected to continue for three weeks.

World.title: Man tells jury he saw farmer accused of triple murder shoot family
World.content:
The trial of a Queensland cattle farmer accused of a triple murder and an attempted murder in 2022 has heard from a man who says he witnessed the shooting and survived a bullet wound himself.

Darryl Valroy Young, 63, pleaded not guilty to three counts of murder and one count of attempted murder in the Supreme Court in Townsville.

The jury trial, expected to run for three weeks, has heard the Bogie farmer and owner of Shannonvale Station is accused of killing his neighbour Graham Tighe, as well as Mr Tighe's mother Maree Schwarz and stepfather Mervyn Schwarz by shooting each of them with a rifle.

Darryl Valroy Young took notes with pen and paper as Ross Tighe gave evidence. (ABC News: Carole Howlett)

The trial has also heard that Mr Young is accused of shooting Graham's brother, Ross Tighe, who survived the incident on August 4, 2022.

Mr Young's defence lawyer has argued the farmer never saw the family he is accused of shooting on the day of the alleged incident.

Ross Tighe, 34, gave evidence on Tuesday via video link from a courtroom in Mackay, south of Townsville.

He told the court the family took two utes to meet Mr Young at the gate of Shannonvale Station on the day of the alleged shooting where there was a tense exchange.

Ross Tighe told the court he saw Mr Young shoot Maree Schwarz and Mervyn Schwarz (pictured) with a rifle. (Supplied)

Brother describes shooting

He said Mr Young refused to shake Mervyn Schwarz's hand and then retrieved a rifle from the back seat of his ute and began firing.

"He shot Merv in the face — then I turned around to start running," Mr Tighe said.

"I ran between the utes to get behind them for cover — when I turned, I'm pretty sure I got shot in the stomach and it went into my hip.

"I saw Graham had been shot as well on the ground towards the back of the utes."

Ross Tighe said he saw Mr Young shoot his brother Graham Tighe (pictured). (Facebook)

Mr Tighe told the court he then looked for his mother.

"She had been shot, she was sort of on her knees, hiding her stomach," he said.

'I knew they were dead'

Mr Tighe said after the shooting he ran downhill in an attempt to hide from Mr Young.

"I tried to run, my right leg kept falling over, I fell down like five or six times trying to get to where I ran towards," he said.

"I was running and when I stopped to lie down to hide I heard two more gunshots.

"I tried to cover myself with grass really quickly."

He said after about10 minutes he returned to the gate and heard the engine of one of his family's two utes running.

"I knew they were all going to be dead so I was trying not to look, I didn't look for mum and then I opened the car door because the ignition was on and she was there," he said.

"She was f**king shot … through the window."

Mr Tighe said he drove away in another car, found help and was taken to Mackay Base Hospital via rescue helicopter.

Cattle accusations

The trial heard Mr Young's Shannonvale Station shared a boundary with Sutherland Station which was jointly owned by Mervyn Schwarz, Maree Schwarz and Graham Tighe.

Ross Tighe said there was an unfenced area where the cattle stations met.

He said that Mr Young had accused his brother, Graham Tighe, of causing stress to cattle by "galloping them".

He said that on the morning of the alleged shooting Mr Young accused the family of stealing his calves.

Ross Tighe told the court that no cattle had been galloped, nor were any calves stolen.

He also denied he or his family members were armed on that day.

Ross Tighe told the court he ran away from Darryl Valroy Young as he fired bullets from a rifle. (ABC News: Carole Howlett)

Cross examination begins

Mr Young's defence lawyer Anthony J Kimmins began to cross examine Ross Tighe on Tuesday.

He asked Mr Tighe about the cattle business his family ran.

Mr Tighe explained he was a manager of a 10,500 acre cattle station in Roma which, like Sutherland Station at Bogie, was owned by his brother, stepfather and mother.

He said his family owned a property at Tara and two smaller properties but said he was not on any property titles.

He said he took a weekly wage for his role in the family business as did his partner at the time and had endeavoured to purchase one of the family's smaller properties.

Mr Kimmins also questioned Mr Tighe about a short pigging trip he went on with Mr Young and his son Derrick Young as well as a fence, kilometres in length, which the families installed together.

Cross examination of Mr Tighe will resume on Wednesday.

The trial continues.

World.title: The RBA's best guess is that it's done hiking interest rates
World.content:
Every second meeting, the Reserve Bank's boffins produce a set of economic forecasts that guides the board's thinking for the next three months.

The latest set of forecasts is good news for mortgage borrowers fearing further rate hikes.

Inflation was dramatically lower than the RBA expected just three months ago in May, even though oil prices behaved much as expected.

What's more, the bank continues to expect inflation to fall to the mid-point of its 2-3 per cent target range by the end of 2027, even though rates are tipped to be lower.

The RBA uses market pricing for future interest rates in its forecasts, so as not to given any hints about its own forward view, and traders now expect the cash rate to be about the same at the end of the forecast period in December 2028 as it is now — 4.35 per cent.

RBA keeps rate at 4.35pc The Reserve Bank has kept interest rates on hold at its August meeting, after three rate hikes earlier this year.

The Reserve Bank's governor Michele Bullock, learning from the mistakes of her predecessor Philip Lowe, is always reticent about giving so-called forward guidance on interest rates, that is a view on where they'll likely be at some point in the future.

At today's press conference, she came about as close to doing so as I have ever heard.

Referring to the bank's forecast that inflation would be at the mid-point of the target band by the end of 2027, she said, "This is a reasonable time to get inflation back down to target."

Reading between the lines, that tells you that if the economy continues tracking close to the RBA's current forecasts then it will see no need for further rate rises.

The RBA's forecasts show it thinks inflation will return to target with the current cash rate. (AAP: Joel Carrett)

'May be a need for further interest rate rises'

But before borrowers break out the champagne, or trade the baked beans for Wagyu and shiraz, Ms Bullock used much of her press conference to emphasise that higher rates aren't off the table just yet.

Loading...

"We'll still need to see some further progress before the board can be confident we're going to get inflation back to target with current monetary policy settings," she said.

"In waiting, the board isn't ruling out there may be a need for further interest rate rises if we look like we're off a path that takes us with inflation remaining above the target for much longer in the forecasts."

Just to make sure there was no doubt, Ms Bullock reiterated that a reduction in rates was not even discussed at the board meeting, as well as offering her personal view.

" We already raised three times, and we will go again if we need to. And I think personally that it's quite possible we may need to go, but we will wait and see what the data tells us. "

For those of us attending the Statement on Monetary Policy and briefed by the RBA's chief economist Sarah Hunter, it's clear why Michele Bullock is at pains to keep a rate hike firmly on the table.

There's a litany of upside risks to the RBA's inflation forecasts, the realisation of any of which could delay the return to target beyond a "reasonable time" and see the bank hike again.

The global economy could keep growing more strongly than expected.

The Middle East oil crisis could flare up or keep dragging on, sending oil prices back over $US100 a barrel.

The energy price shock we've already had might only just be filtering through to broader price rises, especially with the fuel excise cut having temporarily mitigated some of the pain.

The major risks to the central bank's inflation forecasts, including the Middle East conflict and energy shock, are to the upside. (Reuters: Hamad I Mohammed)

The capacity constraints in the economy could worsen rather than improve, with productivity again going backwards and the RBA lowering its already weak forecasts.

That weak productivity is already evident in stubborn domestic inflation, such as in the services sector, while the data centre construction boom threatens to soak up scarce tradies and push building costs to yet fresh heights.

To top it off, the looming El Niño risks slashing food production and raising prices.

Loading

Complacency the biggest inflation threat

Meanwhile, there's just one major downside risk to inflation identified by the RBA, which is a deeper-than-expected housing market downturn that dents residential building demand and sees nervy home owners close their wallets as prices keep falling.

In the presser, Bullock herself said repeatedly that housing is not the bank's focus right now.

"That isn't really the main game here for us at the moment," she told reporters.

"The main game here for us is excess capacity, tight labour market, particularly in some areas like construction, the Middle East conflict, the AI boom, these are all the things that are front of mind in terms of risks to the inflation outlook."

With most of the risks to the upside, Michele Bullock was most keen to address the greatest risk of all — complacency.

"It's important that people believe we will act if we need to," she said.

ABC Business Daily The podcast that helps you unpack the latest business and finance news.

At this point, the Reserve Bank's greatest enemy is a widespread expectation that there won't be any further rate hikes.

Well-practised in jawboning, the RBA governor was today playing the role of a financial Jaws: "Just when you thought it was safe to go back into the market …", as they would say in the movie.

Bullock knows full well that further rate hikes risk pushing unemployment above 5 per cent and tipping the economy into recession.

The RBA board will take that risk if it has to, but it would rather not.

World.title: Veteran Manly prop Nathan Brown outlines NRL exit plan
World.content:
Manly prop Nathan Brown has revealed he decided at the start of the season this would be his last in the NRL, as the veteran forward eyes a move to the Super League.

Off contract at the end of 2026, Brown has confirmed he will finish up at Manly this year as the Sea Eagles begin a changing of the guard in the forward pack.

Brown's final month at Manly will take on even more importance on Friday night, after he was called in to start for the first time in two years against the Dolphins amid the Sea Eagles' forwards shortage.

The 33-year-old is still hoping to exit the NRL in a finals series, with Manly likely needing to win their last four games to return to the top eight.

Munster free to play Melbourne Storm five-eighth Cameron Munster avoids suspension after the NRL match review committee downgrades his dangerous contact charge from Saturday's win over Manly.

"I just knew it was my time to call it quits in the NRL … I made my debut in 2013, so it's my 14th year. When your time's up, your time is up," Brown told AAP.

"The last thing I wanted to do was sit on the fence with whether I want to stay or go overseas.

"It's just made everything a lot easier to go all in this year and enjoy every moment, every training session and every game."

Brown was regarded as one of the most aggressive forwards in the game when he debuted at Wests Tigers in 2013, as well as during a two-year stint at South Sydney.

Nathan Brown played six seasons at the Eels, making his Origin debut while at the club. (Getty Images: Anthony Au-Yeung)

He came into his own at Parramatta, playing two State of Origins for NSW in 2020 and the 2022 grand final for the Eels before reviving his career with a train-and-trial deal at Manly in 2024.

"I find it funny [looking back at old footage)]" said Brown, who is on track to reach 200 games this month.

"When I started, I was a lot bigger. I wasn't really that fit. I was a bit overweight for my size and my position. And I had a different attitude back then.

"But at the same time, you learn a lot from it. You feel grateful that you had to go through those things."

Brown's NRL retirement comes with fellow veteran Manly prop Siua Taukeiaho off contract after breaking his leg in two places in May.

The Sea Eagles have signed props Davvy Moale and Toni Mataele for next year, while Kayliss Fatialofa will arrive as a highly-heralded second rower.

Teenage prop Simi Laiafi has also shown promise starting this year alongside Taniela Paseka, and looms as a long-term prospect.

Brown said he was proud of the impact he was able to have off the bench this year, still hitting the line with gusto.

"You don't want to be finishing by just clutching at the straws and hanging on by a thread," he said.

ABC Sport Daily podcast ABC Sport Daily is your daily sports conversation. We dive into the biggest story of the day and get you up to speed with everything else that's making headlines.

"I feel like I can probably still physically play another year in the NRL. But in the mental side of things, I'm just ready."

Manly expect to be without prop Paseka for at least a fortnight after he injured his knee against Melbourne last week, in a seismic blow to their finals chances.

Ethan Bullemor (concussion) remains sidelined, while Kobe Hetherington (biceps) last week joined Taukeiaho in being out for the season.

Second-rower Ben Trbojevic (concussion) is also still out, while his superstar brother Tom has been kept on ice for another week in his return from a hamstring injury.

AAP

World.title: Breaking: Canberra Institute of Technology CEO Margot McNeill resigns
World.content:
Canberra Institute of Technology (CIT) chief executive Margot McNeill has resigned from the role after months of pressure to step down.

Dr McNeill's appointment as CIT CEO was brought into question earlier this year after revelations she had failed to disclose an investigation into misconduct in her previous role at TAFE NSW.

In the statement announcing her resignation, Dr McNeill said her decision was "tremendously difficult".

"It has become clear that this decision is in the best interest of the CIT community, especially students and staff, about whom I care deeply. Equally, it is in my best interest, including that of my family," she said.

Dr McNeill was appointed as CEO in June 2025.

In May this year, Dr McNeill came under further pressure to resign after an ACT Legislative Assembly inquiry found she "should have disclosed the information about the misconduct investigation or findings to the CIT board in a timely manner and that she did not".

Dr McNeill had repeatedly said she was under a strict obligation not to share the existence of the investigation, but TAFE NSW has publicly contradicted that.

Her evidence before the initial committee triggered another assembly probe, which questioned whether Dr McNeill had misled the assembly.

Its findings, released last week, criticised Dr McNeill as having been "deliberately obstructive" and "combative".

Mitch Pirie has been appointed the acting CEO of CIT. (LinkedIn: Mitch Pirie)

Dr McNeill has been on extended leave amid the controversy.

On Friday last week, Mitch Pirie was appointed acting CEO.

Until now he has been the ACT government's acting deputy under treasurer.

In a statement about her resignation, Dr McNeill said it had been "a source of great pride" to lead the "much-loved Canberra institution.

"Sector leaders encouraged me to apply for this role in recognition of my extensive expertise in tertiary harmonisation and education excellence," she said.

"It was a dream opportunity to use my experience and leadership to position CIT as a hub for innovation during such an exciting period in tertiary education transformation."

Dr McNeill added that she continued to be passionate about the value of the vocational education and training sector, which she had "dedicated 40 years of [her] life to".

World.title: Wildberries warehouse ablaze, 13 killed as Russia, Ukraine trade fire
World.content:
Thirteen people have been killed and a Wildberries warehouse set ablaze as Russia and Ukraine traded attacks on Tuesday, local time.

Russian attacks killed six people and wounded 20 in the south-eastern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia and also struck Kyiv, triggering fires in the capital, officials said.

Zaporizhzhia regional governor Ivan Fedorov said Russian troops launched missiles and aerial bombs at the city. He posted pictures showing buildings and vehicles ablaze.

Air raid alerts were sounded in both Zaporizhzhia and in Kyiv, where the capital's military administration said warehouses in a central district were ablaze. One person was reported injured.

Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces had carried out overnight strikes on military-related transport and logistics centres in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv and on a major iron and steel works it said was helping Ukraine's war effort in Zaporizhzhia.

Elsewhere in Ukraine, local authorities reported another six people were killed and 16 wounded in the regions of Dnipropetrovsk and Donetsk.

Ukrainian attack kills one, triggers Wildberries fire

A drone attack killed one person and injured two others in Russia's Voronezh region, while falling debris triggered fires at a Wildberries warehouse, regional governor Alexander Gusev and the company said.

North Korea benefits from Russia alliance Almost two weeks ago, what is believed to be a North Korean missile was fired in an attack that killed a Ukrainian family. It could be part of a major escalation in North Korea's involvement in the war in Ukraine.

Russia's air defence units destroyed 15 drones over the city of Voronezh and five districts of the region, Mr Gusev said on Telegram.

"A drone crash caused fires at two warehouses of a large company. At one facility, the fire has been contained to an area of 16,000 square metres, while at the other, a blaze covering 20,000 square metres is being extinguished. Emergency services are on scene," the governor said.

Earlier on Tuesday, Russian online retailer Wildberries said its logistics facilities in the Voronezh region had been evacuated in accordance with safety requirements.

It later said that the fire at the facility had been extinguished, that goods had not been damaged and that deliveries had been rerouted to other warehouses.

Local governor Yevgeny Solntsev also said an industrial enterprise was on fire in Russia's Orenburg region after an attack by "enemy drones". There had been no reports of casualties, he said.

The Ukrainian military said it had attacked an oil refinery in Orsk, located in the Orenburg region.

Reuters

World.title: ‘Pitiful’: Perth mum to appeal after DV thug sentenced without magistrate viewing crucial CCTV footage
World.content:
Exclusive NationalWACourts ‘Pitiful’: Perth mum to appeal after DV thug sentenced without magistrate viewing crucial CCTV footage Rebecca Peppiatt August 11, 2026 — 7:13pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Warning: This story contains graphic content. A Perth woman who fled the country with her children after a horrific domestic violence assault by her partner has been left reeling after he was given a “pitiful” sentence over the attack that forced her to uproot her life. Chloe Wright was assaulted by her ex-partner, Guy Cramp. Guy Cramp was charged after he bashed the mother of his newborn son at her home in Stratton in November last year. At the time, he had been out of prison for five days, having being jailed for violently assaulting a taxi driver over a $20 fare.



Chloe Wright had been in a relationship with Cramp, with whom she shares a child, for 18 months when she told him she was going out for the evening with a friend. Cramp, 33, who had twice previously been jailed for violently assaulting two previous partners and been convicted for assaulting his own parents, lashed out at Wright “out of jealousy”, punching her in the face as she held their son while sitting on the sofa. Loading That was the extent of the information that police prosecutors gave to Magistrate Paul Lyons ahead of Cramp’s sentencing on Tuesday. The full extent of a horrifying and protracted assault that continued outside Wright’s home and captured by her CCTV cameras was never presented to the court.



“I have not been given the CCTV footage and I have not seen it,” Lyons said on Tuesday. Why he was not given the confronting footage to view was not made clear, but prosecutors previously told the court they did not know the extent of Wright’s injuries, while only one small aspect of the assault was outlined. Were it not for her victim impact statement, the court would have been given no knowledge of the extent of Cramp’s attack that resulted in a broken nose and cheekbone, and a lengthy wait for surgery to repair the damage. Wright was also placed into protection by the Department of Communities with her children when Cramp was released on bail in February to complete a domestic violence offenders’ program. He failed to participate in even half of the court-ordered sessions, and later cut off his ankle monitoring bracelet and fled from police, evading capture for 12 hours and sending Wright into a terrifying lockdown.



“I have to have a rhinoplasty and a septoplasty, and I’m on the wait list at Royal Perth [Hospital] – none of that was brought up by the prosecution,” Wright said outside court on Tuesday. Chloe Wright needed surgery after the attack. “It seemed because I wasn’t stabbed or permanently deformed that I didn’t matter, and what I’ve done doesn’t matter, and I’ve had to change everything in my life. It’s so, it’s so wrong. “Maybe I just shouldn’t have come forward. What was the point?” Wright released the footage to the media earlier this year to raise awareness of how domestic violence perpetrators are dealt with by the courts. The vision, which shows Cramp assaulting Wright while holding their newborn son, went viral.



“The prosecution should have made sure that that judge was able to see that footage,” she said. Related Article Exclusive

Courts ‘My baby was covered in my blood’: Perth mum confronts serial DV attacker in court “Australia has seen that footage. Why has the [magistrate] not seen that footage?” Cramp was sentenced to 15 months in prison for the assault on Wright, and eight months for cutting off his ankle monitoring bracelet. He was made eligible for parole, which means he could be released in March next year due to time already served.



He was also placed on the serial domestic violence register. Wright called the sentence “pitiful” and plans to lodge a formal complaint with WA Police and lobby for an appeal.

World.title: Why Grand Theft Auto’s Netflix deal is creating controversy
World.content:
Analysis TechnologyVideo games Why Grand Theft Auto’s Netflix deal is creating controversy Tim Biggs August 11, 2026 — 7:10pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

With unprecedented blockbuster Grand Theft Auto VI just three months away, anticipation is building among players who are yet to see a decent representation of what the game actually is. But while publisher Rockstar recently confirmed that an “extended look” was coming on August 28, one detail in particular has caused a stir: the video will premiere on Netflix. No details have been given on what the presentation will include, or how long it will be, although Rockstar has said the video will be available on YouTube and its own website six hours after the premiere. Still, this is uncharted territory for promoting a video game. Generally, prerelease videos are disseminated as accessibly as possible because the publisher needs to drum up hype. Here, Rockstar is saying its first in-depth look at the game is a product unto itself, worthy of a platform that people pay up to $29 a month for. The afternoon premiere in the US, which will mean the video is exclusive to Netflix at prime-time, will result in the video appearing at 5am in Australia. And Rockstar is not unjustified in its confidence. Grand Theft Auto V was a massive hit that topped bestseller charts for more than 10 years, and is the biggest entertainment product in history by practically any metric. The 2013 game has sold 230 million copies to date, making more than $14 billion in revenue. Despite consumer backlash over Rockstar’s decision to launch Grand Theft Auto VI as a $130 digital-only game — with no option to buy it on disc — and its decision to lock certain gameplay elements and features behind a $160 Ultimate Edition, pre-orders for the game have been off the charts.



At a quarterly earnings call last week, Rockstar parent Take-Two reported $US1.4 billion ($1.98 billion) in net bookings, which considering previous reports and its current slate of games, might indicate that GTA VI pre-orders are on track to make $1.5 billion by launch if they haven’t already. Take-Two chief executive Strauss Zelnick said at the call that the pre-orders had been “unprecedented and astonishing”, but defended the game’s high pricing, saying the company was not aiming to maximise cost to consumer. “The truth is that the real cost of a AAA video game is a whole lot lower today than it was 20 years ago. And our goal is to continue to overdeliver for our consumers because how you feel about any experience is the intersection of the experience itself and what you pay for it,” he said. “So to say that we expect that Grand Theft Auto VI will be an incredible bargain as experiences go is a gross understatement because Rockstar Games is known for overdelivering.” Dozens of vehicles, guns, cosmetic items and in-game shops will be exclusive to the more expensive Ultimate Edition. As with the high cost, debuting new footage exclusively on Netflix will not ultimately hurt the game. But it does feed into an undertone of negativity surrounding GTA VI from some players and commentators, who take issue with Rockstar’s hubris. The game, which has been estimated to have cost about $US2 billion ($2.9 billion) to develop, is destined to be close to the most lucrative media product of all time based on game sales alone. Does it really need to squeeze people with extra paid content at launch, or accept undoubtedly massive stacks of cash from Netflix as well?



“The next few months are going to be a parade of marketing bullshit they wouldn’t dare try if it were any game other than GTA,” said writer David Smith on Bluesky, reacting to the Netflix news. “This is unbelievably scummy ... This needs to be called out because if any other studio such as Bethesda did this they would be crucified,” said @BaileyPoints on X. View post on X Still, not every voice was so critical, especially on forums dedicated to GTA hype. People are desperate to see more of this modernised Bonnie and Clyde story, its fictionalised satirical version of Florida, and the huge assortment of vehicles, guns, locations and activities. “Waited 13 years, but can’t wait 6 hours longer,” said Reddit user Bong55555 sarcastically in response to the complaints.



“They used to do specials, ‘making-ofs’, and other stuff on network tv to build hype back in the day. Mainly for blockbuster movies. Nice to see it still exists for those that care,” said user buttbuttlolbuttbutt in the same thread. Regardless, the deal speaks to how both Netflix and Rockstar see themselves, and the direction in which games may be moving within wider culture. Netflix has begun including certain mobile games – including from Rockstar – with its subscriptions, and bringing streamed game experiences to its TV app. But it’s also increasingly selling its ability to host live events, including sports and concerts. The GTA VI premiere allows it to flex both angles, tying the Netflix brand to a much-anticipated milestone in mainstream gaming. Editor's pick Analysis

Video games Consumer rights lost in the digital media age are unlikely to come back For Rockstar, which knows that practically anybody who seeks out game trailers is already planning to buy GTA VI, Netflix could be a door to a wider audience that isn’t even aware of the game. Netflix has 325 million subscribers globally, a tiny fraction of the potential audience on YouTube. But a big chunk of that base may be immune to online game advertising, with Netflix being the place they go for movies and TV. The presentation will undoubtedly be heavily promoted, and appear at the top of the service’s trending lists.



A similarly meteoric run to Grand Theft Auto V is not guaranteed this time around. That game arrived at the end of the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 era, when consoles were cheap, and it was then able to re-release on more powerful hardware as a definitive version of an already celebrated game. This time, although the Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5 have been out for almost six years, hardware prices are going up thanks to the dire component shortages caused by AI infrastructure build-outs. While sales at launch will be strong, Rockstar may ultimately end up relying on companies like Netflix to support its massive game over the next 10 years, if the bulk of casual video game consumers are priced out of the console market and turn to mobile and streaming.
